reference: Jenkins, Ryan and Lorenzo Nericcio. “Exploring Methods for Impact Quantification.” Report funded by Center for Advancing Safety of Machine Intelligence (casmi). July, 2023
title: Evaluating Metrics for Impact Quantification
affiliations: California Polytechnic State University and San Diego State University - College of Arts and Letters

detail.title: Evaluating Metrics for Impact Quantification

publicationDetails.detailsText: Jenkins, Ryan and Lorenzo Nericcio. “Exploring Methods for Impact Quantification.” Report funded by Center for Advancing Safety of Machine Intelligence (casmi). July, 2023

detail.abstract:
This project proposes concrete metrics to assess the human impact of machine learning applications, thus addressing the gap between ethics and quantitative measurement. Current discussions of AI ethics revolve around fairness, accountability, transparency, and explainability (the so-called “fate” principles), yet lack concrete metrics for practically implementing or measur- ing the ethical dimensions of AI. Our report proposes such metrics, defends their philosophical foundations, and illustrates how they can be implemented to facilitate analysis and decision making throughout an organization. We improve upon existing risk assessments of AI, moving us closer to the goal of precise, quantitative assessment of AI’s human impacts.

We outline a universal theory of human flourishing, based on Martha Nussbaum and Amartya Sen’s “capabilities approach.” This theory encom- passes broad categories such as environmental health, bodily health, and free- dom of affiliation. The approach’s wide scope and “ecumenical” nature allows us to circumvent contentious debates about what constitutes a good life while accommodating a broad array of reasonable views.

Next, we suggest selecting relevant capabilities that align with the goal of the domain wherein the AI model is deployed.

Last, we identify relevant metrics to measure an application’s impact on human flourishing and propose a “Human Impact Scorecard” that can include both qualitative and quantitative metrics. These scorecards allow for comparisons between applications, thus enabling informed decision-making. We illustrate this approach by applying it to three real-world case studies.

The report, up until this point, stands on its own. If a reader is curious about our methodology, in the latter portion of the report, we explore the philosoph- ical foundations, adjacent approaches, and previous work that informs our approach. This analysis reveals several philosophical challenges confronting multidimensional measures of human wellbeing, against which we establish requirements for a successful approach. We show how our approach satisfies these requirements better than any competing approach we know of.

Finally, we discuss potential extensions of this work, like accommodating a broader sociotechnical analysis of AI models and addressing other species of harm that might be caused by AI systems.

title: The LAAM Framework: Operationalizing Fairness in Asymmetric Enforcement Systems

detail.title: The LAAM Framework: Operationalizing Fairness in Asymmetric Enforcement Systems
detail.abstract:
Regulatory audits are widely assumed to be neutral oversight tools, yet their structure often embeds systemic bias. This paper introduces the Lopez Theory of Asymmetric Enforcement (LTAE), a game-theoretic framework that exposes and corrects institutional asymmetries across taxation, healthcare, labor, and AI governance. Drawing from firsthand audit experience and formal modeling, I present the Lopez Audit Anchor Model (LAAM)—a fairness-aware architecture that embeds strategic memory, anchor decay, and Bayesian belief updates to recalibrate enforcement dynamics.

LAAM transforms audits from punitive, memory-less cycles into dynamic games that learn, forgive, and adapt. It penalizes false positives, rewards corrective behavior, and introduces transparency through override logging. The framework is implemented in Python and supported by an open-source audit simulator, enabling empirical testing of its core hypotheses. Simulations suggest LAAM can reduce redundant audits by over 40%, increase voluntary compliance, and foster a cooperative Nash equilibrium where fairness becomes the rational strategy for both auditors and auditees.

This paper bridges AI system design, game theory, and public policy, offering a modular toolkit for regulators, engineers, and compliance professionals seeking to operationalize fairness. It is not just a theory—it is a prototype, a provocation, and a call to reimagine enforcement as a strategic system of trust.

title: Identification and Estimation of Continuous-Time Job Search Models with Preference Shocks
affiliations: Duke University - Department of Economics, Bank of Portugal, Duke University - Department of Economics and Amazon.com

detail.title: Identification and Estimation of Continuous-Time Job Search Models with Preference Shocks

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper applies some of the key insights of dynamic discrete choice models to continuous-time job search models. Our framework incorporates preference shocks into search models, resulting in a tight connection between value functions and conditional choice probabilities. In this environment, we establish constructive identification of the model parameters, including the wage offer distributions off-and on-the-job. Our framework makes it possible to estimate nonstationary search models in a simple and tractable way, without having to solve any differential equations. We apply our method using Hungarian administrative data. Longer unemployment durations are associated with lower offer arrival rates, resulting in accepted wages falling over time. Counterfactual simulations indicate that increasing unemployment benefits by 90 days results in a 14-day increase in expected unemployment duration.

title: Educating Entrepreneurs on VC Contracts
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Department of Finance, HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong and HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Educating Entrepreneurs on VC Contracts
detail.abstract: We conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the impact of contract education and contract legal consulting on entrepreneurs' outcomes in venture capital (VC) and seed funding. Entrepreneurs in the treatment group received targeted instruction in VC contract terms and startup financing agreements. We find that educated entrepreneurs are less likely to secure initial angel or seed funding and are more likely to pursue traditional employment rather than continue with their startup ventures. However, among those who do obtain angel and VC investment, treated entrepreneurs are more likely to receive subsequent funding rounds, achieve higher valuation in later stages, and experience a lower risk of involuntary removal as cofounders. These findings suggest that increased contract knowledge enables entrepreneurs to make more informed career choices and negotiate more favorable terms, albeit at the cost of reduced entry into the VC funding pipeline.

title: Integrating Emotional and Cognitive Biases in Graded Decision-making Models: Insights From a Theoretical Case Study in Healthcare
affiliations: School of Economics and Management of the University of Bologna

detail.title: Integrating Emotional and Cognitive Biases in Graded Decision-making Models: Insights From a Theoretical Case Study in Healthcare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No fund received

detail.abstract: Classical decision theory has long been anchored in the ideal of the rational actor, guided by internally consistent preferences and the axioms of Expected Utility Theory (EUT). Behavioral economics and cognitive psychology have enriched this framework by revealing systematic deviations driven by cognitive biases, while affective science has exposed the profound role of emotional states in shaping perception, valuation, and choice. Yet, in most formal models, cognition and emotion remain analytically segregated, treated as distinct modifiers rather than dynamically coupled determinants of behavior. This paper introduces the Integrated Behavioral Decision-Making Model (IBDM), a formal, parameterized framework that unifies graded emotional states and cognitive distortions into a single utility structure. Drawing inspiration from Vernon L. Smith's reinterpretation of Adam Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments, the IBDM incorporates the boundedness of human rationality not as a deviation from a normative standard, but as a structural feature of decision-making. Fear and optimism are modeled as graded intensities that interact multiplicatively with cognitive biases such as loss aversion and anchoring, altering decision utility in nonlinear and path-dependent ways. A theoretical case study in healthcare decision-making, whether to undergo high-risk surgery, is simulated using Python. Results demonstrate that small changes in emotional intensity can reverse predicted preferences under traditional models, revealing regions of decision-space where affective forces dominate over risk-return trade-offs. This insight reframes the design of interventions in personalized medicine and public health, highlighting the necessity of emotionally intelligent policy tools. The IBDM is not merely a theoretical innovation: it is an epistemic bridge between normative theory, empirical behavioral evidence, and the lived emotional realities of decision contexts. It provides a blueprint for experimental validation, cross-disciplinary integration, and the next generation of computational behavioral models.

title: Protocol for Afterschool Rx  2.0: a pilot randomized crossover trial to determine the feasibility of prescriptions to afterschool care for children with cardiovascular risk factors
affiliations: Augusta University, , , Augusta University and University of South Carolina - Arnold School of Public Health

detail.title: Protocol for Afterschool Rx  2.0: a pilot randomized crossover trial to determine the feasibility of prescriptions to afterschool care for children with cardiovascular risk factors
detail.abstract: Background: CVD risk factors childhood, including obesity and hypertension, can be mitigated with physical activity and a healthy diet. After school programs provide an important opportunity to increase physical activity and improve cardiovascular health. Afterschool Rx is an innovative referral and voucher program that enables healthcare providers to prescribe free afterschool care for children with CVD risk factors from families at or below 250% of the federal poverty level.Methods: This study will employ an ORBIT Phase IIb, randomized crossover design to conduct a preliminary trial of Afterschool Rx. Participating children (ages 6-11 years old; n=48) will be randomly assigned to attend afterschool care in either the fall or spring semester, with the opposite semester will serve as the comparison period (afterschool-as-usual). Vouchers will cover the cost of attending afterschool care at existing community-based programs (e.g., YMCA, Boys and Girls Clubs). Primary outcomes will examine the reach and potential dissemination of the program using the PRISM/REAIM Framework. Exploratory outcomes include health behaviors (e.g., physical activity, inactivity, sleep, screen use, and diet quality) and cardiovascular health indicators (e.g., cardiorespiratory fitness, blood glucose, blood pressure, HbA1c, and cholesterol levels). Exploratory analyses will examine the difference in within-person change between semesters.Discussion: This study will be the first randomized, controlled trial to evaluate the reach and feasibility of dissemination for prescribing afterschool care as a clinical strategy for addressing cardiovascular risk factors. Results will inform additional testing and development of the Afterschool Rx intervention.

detail.abstract: This paper presents Green Aid™, a public-attitude-based environmental tax relief designed to transform voluntary environmental participation into measurable climate outcomes. The model integrates fiscal incentives, behavioural economics, and species-level ecological valuation through the original Green Economic Model of Giving (GEMG). It introduces three dynamic functions—participation, cost, and environmental benefit—supported by two operational metrics: Participation Absorption Capacity (PAC) and Participation Unit Cost (PUC). Using case studies from the London Urban Forest and Aguzzano Park, the paper demonstrates how voluntary contributions matched by government can deliver transparent, effective, low-cost climate action. The scheme is pilot-ready for the United Kingdom and addresses structural failures highlighted at Belém, offering a domestic, trust-building alternative to traditional carbon markets and international offset mechanisms.

title: Insider Trading and Position Limits
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - School of Law

detail.title: Insider Trading and Position Limits

publicationDetails.detailsText: UCLA School of Law, Law-Econ Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: University of California, Los Angeles School of Law, Law & Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Federal law has long prohibited insider trading in securities such as stocks and bonds. Yet many other financial assets-particularly derivatives and commodities-have historically fallen outside those rules. This Article asks why insider trading is penalized for some assets but not others. It argues that the goals of insider trading law are often pursued through alternative mechanisms. Markets lacking insider trading prohibitions are not unregulated; rather, they are governed by substitute regimes that achieve similar ends through different means. By examining the relationship between securities insider trading law and derivatives position limits, this Article clarifies the function of insider trading regulation and illuminates its boundaries. It shows that position-limit rules, though rarely analyzed in this way, can serve as functional substitutes for insider trading restrictions, offering a broader perspective on how law manages informed trading across markets.

title: The Cost of Paralysis: Economic and Industrial Impacts of the October 2025 Government Shutdown

detail.title: The Cost of Paralysis: Economic and Industrial Impacts of the October 2025 Government Shutdown
detail.abstract: The October 2025 federal government shutdown, now entering its fourth week, represents the latest manifestation of a structural governance dysfunction that threatens American industrial competitiveness and national resilience. This paper analyses the cascading economic impacts of the shutdown in federal workforce disruption, healthcare system stress, and industrial sector damage. While comprehensive cost estimates for the ongoing October 2025 shutdown are still being compiled, historical precedent provides a baseline for projections. The Congressional Budget Office estimated that the 35-day shutdown in 2018-2019 cost the U.S. economy $11 billion, including $3 billion in permanent losses (CBO, 2019). Scaled to the current shutdown's scope and duration, preliminary estimates suggest direct costs could exceed $6 billion with additional multiplier effects.Through comparative analysis with international budget processes and systematic evaluation of policy alternatives, we demonstrate that the United States' unique susceptibility to shutdown crises constitutes a self-inflicted competitive disadvantage during a critical period of great power competition and economic transformation. Our framework proposes immediate actions to resolve the current impasse alongside short-term and long-term structural reforms including automatic continuing resolutions, budget process modernization, and elimination of redundant crisis mechanisms. The analysis positions governance reform not as a partisan priority but as an industrial policy imperative: America's competitors do not paralyse their governments, and sustained economic leadership requires institutional capabilities matching our technological and entrepreneurial strengths.

title: ENDOGENOUS OXYTOCIN AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH EATING BEHAVIOR AND METABOLIC HEALTH: A BAYESIAN TARGET-TRIAL EMULATION
affiliations: , , , ,  and

detail.title: ENDOGENOUS OXYTOCIN AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH EATING BEHAVIOR AND METABOLIC HEALTH: A BAYESIAN TARGET-TRIAL EMULATION
detail.abstract: Background:Beyond its classical reproductive and social functions, the neuropeptide oxytocin has been hypothesized to influence eating behavior and metabolic regulation, though most human evidence remains correlational.Objective:To estimate causal-compatible associations between endogenous plasma oxytocin concentrations and key behavioral and metabolic outcomes using a Bayesian target-trial emulation framework, while accounting for measured confounding and model uncertainty.Methods:In a cohort of 99 adults examined at the Republican Specialized Scientific-Practical Medical Center of Endocrinology (Tashkent, Uzbekistan), we emulated a two-arm trial comparing high (≥ 37.6 pg/mL) versus low (< 37.6 pg/mL) plasma oxytocin concentrations. Bayesian augmented inverse-probability weighting with overlap weighting (adjusting for age, sex, and BMI) estimated posterior associations for disordered-eating severity (Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire [EDE-Q] global score) and metabolic indices—the hepatic steatosis index (HSI) and visceral adiposity index (VAI). Restricted cubic-spline models examined continuous dose–response relationships.Results:The emulation yielded a strong and precise association between higher oxytocin and lower EDE-Q scores (posterior mean ATE = –1.20; 94 % HDI = –1.65 to –0.75; P(ATE < 0) = 1.000). Estimates for HSI and VAI were directionally beneficial but imprecise. Spline modeling suggested a monotonic reduction in EDE-Q scores across the 80–120 pg/mL oxytocin range.Conclusions:Within a causal-emulation framework, higher endogenous oxytocin concentrations were consistently aligned with healthier behavioral–metabolic profiles.Findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in longitudinal or interventional studies, but they highlight oxytocin as a candidate biomarker of behavioral–metabolic integration.

reference: İzmir İktisat Dergisi, volume 40, issue 1, 2025[10.24988/ije.1472312]
title: Comparative Analysis of OECD Countries Based on Energy Trilemma Index: A Clustering Approach

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of OECD Countries Based on Energy Trilemma Index: A Clustering Approach

publicationDetails.detailsText: İzmir İktisat Dergisi, volume 40, issue 1, 2025[10.24988/ije.1472312]

detail.abstract: This study analyzes OECD countries in the context of the energy trilemma index and clusters countries with similar characteristics. In the study, the k-means clustering technique is used. The optimum number of clusters was determined using the Elbow method in combination with the Silhouette Index. Moreover, all results are visualized to enhance comprehensibility. The results show that countries such as Austria, Canada, Finland, and Denmark are in the high energy trilemma group with index scores of 82.2, 82.3, 82.7, and 83.3, respectively. Countries in the high group have achieved a high level of balance between energy security, energy equity, and environmental sustainability. In addition, countries such as Belgium, Hungary, Australia, the Czech Republic, and Estonia are in the medium energy trilemma group with index scores of 76.4, 76.6, 77.1, 77.6, and 78.7, respectively. Countries in the medium group have made progress in balancing the dimensions of the energy trilemma but have not yet reached excellence. However, countries such as Mexico, Türkiye, Colombia, and Costa Rica are in the low energy trilemma group with index scores of 63.1, 64.1, 64.8, and 69.3, respectively. These low energy trilemma group countries face significant challenges in balancing energy security, energy equity, and environmental sustainability and need to make improvements in these areas.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12319
title: Fact-Checking and Misinformation: Evidence from the Market Leader
affiliations: , SciencesPo - Department of Economics, SciencesPo - Department of Economics, SciencesPo - Department of Economics and University of Liège - HEC Liège

detail.title: Fact-Checking and Misinformation: Evidence from the Market Leader

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: What are the dynamic effects of fact-checking on the behavior of those who circulate misinformation and on the spread of false news? In this paper, we provide causal evidence on these questions, building on a unique partnership with the Agence France Presse (AFP), the world’s largest fact-checking organization and a partner of Facebook’s Third-Party Fact-Checking Program. Over an 18-month period (December 2021-June 2023), we collected information on the stories proposed by fact-checkers during the daily editorial meetings, some of which were ultimately fact-checked while others, despite being ex ante “similar”, were left aside. Using two complementary Difference-in-Differences approaches, one at the story level and the other at the post level (within fact-checked stories), we show that fact-checking reduces the circulation of misinformation on Facebook by approximately 8%, an effect driven entirely by stories rated as “False.” Furthermore, we provide evidence of behavioral responses: the publication of a fact-check more than doubles the deletion of posts in the fact-checked stories, and users whose posts appear in fact-checked stories become less likely to share misinformation in the future. While our results clearly confirm the effectiveness of fact-checking, we provide policy recommendations to further strengthen its impact.

reference: Asian Economic Papers
title: Economic Analysis of Ethical Principles for AI Algorithms: An Autonomous Driving Case
affiliations: Chonnam National University - Department of Economics and Chonnam National University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Economic Analysis of Ethical Principles for AI Algorithms: An Autonomous Driving Case
detail.abstract: This paper develops an economic framework to evaluate ethical principles for autonomous driving vehicle (ADV) algorithms in trolley-type accident scenarios. We compare three candidate social rules-the utilitarian rule, the Rawlsian max-min rule, and the passenger priority rule-by embedding them into a heterogeneous agents model in which citizens alternate between being ADV passengers and pedestrians. We provide algorithms that implement the three rules, and show that the utilitarian rule is weakly superior in terms of maximizing social welfare, though under specific parameter conditions the Rawlsian and passenger priority rules converge to equivalent outcomes. Policy implications are twofold: first, governments must select and enforce a single social rule to avoid coordination failures; second, complementary instruments such as subsidies can align adoption incentives with welfare maximization. The analysis further highlights that cultural orientations, such as the stronger utilitarian tendencies observed in East Asian societies, may affect the ease of implementing optimal policies. By integrating ethical theory, risk quantification, and adoption dynamics, the study provides a unified economic perspective on the governance of ADV ethics.

title: The Impact of a Self-Efficacy-Based Intervention on Intentions to Eat Healthfully: The roles of Motivation and Optimism
affiliations: University of New England and

detail.title: The Impact of a Self-Efficacy-Based Intervention on Intentions to Eat Healthfully: The roles of Motivation and Optimism
detail.abstract: An individual's self-efficacy for healthy eating, the belief in one’s ability to eat healthfully, may lead to intentions to eat healthfully. This study examined whether an intervention intended to build self-efficacy for healthy eating results in greater optimism in regard to healthful eating, approach motivation for healthy eating and intentions to eat healthfully. This study also examined whether optimism for healthy eating mediated the impact of the self-efficacy for healthy eating intervention on motivation and intentions. A sample of 151 Australian adults aged 18 to 78 (M = 33.82, SD = 12.22), 73.9% female, were randomly assigned to a self-efficacy for healthy eating intervention or a control group Participants' self-efficacy for healthy eating, optimism, approach motivation and intentions to eat healthfully were then assessed. The self-efficacy for healthy eating intervention led to significantly greater post-test self-efficacy for healthy eating, optimism regarding healthy eating, and intention to eat healthfully, but did not significantly impact approach motivation. Optimism mediated the relationship between the intervention and both approach motivation and intentions. Limitations and implications for dietary interventions are discussed.

title: An Ubuntu Remedy for Cognitive Decolonization of Environmental Degradation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Shanlax International Journal of Arts, Science and Humanities, volume 12, issue 4, 2025[10.34293/sijash.v12i4.8722]

detail.abstract: The issue of environmental degradation globally is considered endemic to human well-being and the environment. This, over the years has attracted various responses from diverse spheres; cultural, religious, and philosophical perspectives. They highlight the role of belief systems in shaping environmental ethics, with much emphasis on stewardship and communitarian values. However, despite all attempts to contain this global issue, persistent psychological barriers, particularly confirmation bias and anchoring bias, continue to hinder progress in addressing environmental degradation. Informed by this problem, this paper examines how these biases in this context built on anthropocentrism, prevent individuals and societies from adopting sustainable behaviors despite global campaigns and awareness of climate change and its effects. Considering that many proposed solutions have failed to adequately address the psychological factors that reinforce environmentally destructive habits, this paper establishes that it is contingent on the lack of a comprehensive approach to recognizing and at the same time overcoming these mental barriers. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes the philosophy of Ubuntu as a remedy for mental decolonization, by encouraging a turn from human-centered thinking to a more interconnected, holistic view of nature. To this end, this study analyses the intersection between psychological biases and environmental ethics, and at the end shows how the Ubuntu philosophy could remedy the problem that exists. The paper argues that by adopting Ubuntu, individuals can deconstruct biases like confirmation and anchoring, which enables them to build a mindset that views the environment as a co-tenant of the Earth rather than a resource for neither exploitation nor abuse. This shift not only addresses the psychological barriers to environmental preservation but also promotes sustainable, ethical practices through a collective sense of responsibility.

reference: Vision Zero Cities: International Journal of Traffic Safety Innovation, Volume 10, 2025, pp. 79–83
title: Breaking the Car-Law Mold: Rethinking Traffic Rules for Bikes

detail.title: Breaking the Car-Law Mold: Rethinking Traffic Rules for Bikes

publicationDetails.detailsText: Vision Zero Cities: International Journal of Traffic Safety Innovation, Volume 10, 2025, pp. 79–83

detail.abstract: U.S. traffic laws continue to treat bicycles as small cars, imposing motor-vehicle-oriented rules on people who are far more similar to pedestrians in size, speed, and vulnerability. This article argues that such car-centric regulation undermines cyclist safety and perpetuates inequitable enforcement. Drawing on historical context, safety research, and policy examples from the United States and abroad, it shows that flexible rules—such as the Idaho Stop, context-dependent sidewalk cycling, and decriminalization of technical violations—reduce crashes and enhance mobility without increasing conflicts. A legal framework that trusts cyclists’ judgment and targets only genuinely harmful behavior would better reflect real-world conditions and produce safer, more humane streets.

title: Development communication for collaborative governance: Empowering women farmers in food independent villages
affiliations: Universitas Muhammadiyah Tangerang

detail.title: Development communication for collaborative governance: Empowering women farmers in food independent villages

keywords: Women farmers groups (KWT) This study received no specific financial support

detail.abstract: Tangerang Regency faces food security challenges due to high poverty rates and nutritional insecurity, particularly in rural areas such as Sodong Village, a pilot site for the Food Independent Village Program. Despite its considerable agricultural potential, the village encounters obstacles including limited resources, low community participation, and suboptimal communication strategies in the empowerment of Women Farmers Groups (Kelompok Wanita Tani or KWT in Bahasa Indonesia). This study aims to analyze the collaborative governance model in KWT empowerment, evaluate its impact on food security and village socioeconomic welfare, and identify development communication strategies that can strengthen the participation and technical capacity of KWT members. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed, with data collection techniques including in-depth interviews, participant observation, and document analysis. The study in Sodong Village, Tangerang Regency, shows that cross-actor involvement-including the village government, technical agencies, KWT, the community, and the private sector-plays a crucial role in shaping participatory and inclusive governance in the implementation of the Food Independent Village Program. In this context, KWT has transformed into an agent of social change, contributing to increased consumption of nutritious food, higher household income, and strengthened women's roles in local decision-making processes. Identified development communication strategies include interpersonal, digital, institutional, educational, and multi-sectoral communication, which collectively create a dialogical and collaborative ecosystem to foster active participation and enhance the technical capacity of KWT members.

title: A Platform Theory of Nonprofit Pricing and the Nonprofit Platform Lerner Index
affiliations: Samford University - Brock School of Business and California State University, Monterey Bay

detail.title: A Platform Theory of Nonprofit Pricing and the Nonprofit Platform Lerner Index
detail.abstract: This paper develops a novel framework for nonprofit pricing by conceptualizing nonprofits as multi-sided platforms (MSPs) that mediate exchanges between clients and donors. It introduces the Nonprofit Platform Lerner Index (NPLI), a tool that helps nonprofit managers optimize pricing by accounting for both client-price elasticity and donor-side cross-platform effects. The framework demonstrates how nonprofits can strategically leverage donor market power to subsidize client prices, including scenarios where prices fall below marginal cost or become negative. The study reconceptualizes donor engagement activities as core production inputs rather than overhead costs, aligning them with mission-critical objectives. It also explores policy implications, offering insights into antitrust considerations in donor markets. The NPLI provides regulators and managers with a quantitative tool to measure market power across donor and client markets. Future research avenues include empirical validation and applications to nonprofit governance and stakeholder management.

title: Regenerative Capital Systems: A Formal Analysis of Multi-Cycle, Non-Liability Capital Architecture

detail.title: Regenerative Capital Systems: A Formal Analysis of Multi-Cycle, Non-Liability Capital Architecture

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Institutions routinely fail not because they lack resources or expertise, but because their capital cycles are structurally bound to short-horizon fragility cycles—financial volatility, political turnover, capability decay, and civic fluctuation. These fragility cycles operate on timescales fundamentally misaligned with the long-horizon mission cycles that govern asset lifetimes, scientific capability, climate adaptation, and intergenerational public goods. The resulting temporal mismatch produces deterministic capability decline across domains, regardless of managerial competence or policy intent. This paper introduces Regenerative Cycle Architecture (RCA), a general meta-theory of institutional design grounded in the structural separation of cycles. RCA formalises two core operations—cycle decoupling, which renders capital independent of fragility cycles, and cycle alignment, which synchronises capital behaviour with mission cycles. We define a formal ontology of cycles, present a three-layer system model, and derive a set of six structural invariants that are both necessary and jointly sufficient for regenerative, multi-cycle institutional capability. We demonstrate how RCA explains failure patterns across climate adaptation, scientific infrastructure, healthcare systems, civic institutions, and long-lived public assets. We then show that Perpetual Social Capital (PSC) constitutes the first realised instantiation of RCA at the capital layer, providing a mathematically modelled example of non-extractive, non-liability, mission-aligned regenerative capital. RCA further distinguishes between the structural recycling parameter 𝑅 embedded in regenerative architectures and the realised recycling rate 𝑅 observed in empirical deployments. 𝑎 This distinction, developed in subsequent PSC and Alignment Capital work, allows RCA to model the difference between theoretical regenerative capacity and behaviourally achieved alignment. RCA concludes by introducing the cycle constitution, a new category of institutional governance that protects temporal integrity in the same way political constitutions protect power. The paper outlines an interdisciplinary research agenda for RCA as a foundational framework for long-horizon, regenerative institutional design.

title: Understanding Australian Emergency Volunteers: Insights into Retention Based on Motivational Profiles and Leadership Perceptions
affiliations: University of Tasmania

detail.title: Understanding Australian Emergency Volunteers: Insights into Retention Based on Motivational Profiles and Leadership Perceptions
detail.abstract: Emergency volunteers are an indispensable component of disaster response, particularly in regional areas. The recent decline in volunteer numbers, combined with a shift towards more flexible forms of volunteering, poses challenges for emergency management organisations that rely on volunteers to provide emergency responses and brings the issue of volunteer retention into sharp focus. This paper reports on a cluster analysis of the motivations of 455 Australian emergency volunteers, followed by inferential statistics and a qualitative analysis. Three clusters have been identified, each characterised by a unique motivational profile, differing perceptions of leadership, and factors influencing their decisions to continue or cease volunteering. The study highlights the importance of aligning leader behaviours with volunteer expectations and tailoring strategies to the diverse motivational profiles of volunteers. The findings offer emergency management organisations and policymakers a deeper understanding of the contemporary volunteer workforce, which can facilitate recruitment, leadership development, and retention strategies.

title: A Metamorphic Threat: Synthesizing Transformations in the Global Terrorism Landscape
affiliations: ESPIRIDI LLP

detail.title: A Metamorphic Threat: Synthesizing Transformations in the Global Terrorism Landscape
detail.abstract: This systematic review argues that global terrorism is not diminishing but undergoing a profound transformation. Between 2022 and 2025, empirical data reveal a decisive geographic shift, intensifying concentration of violence, and evolving systemic drivers of extremism. Global trends in 2024 show a statistical normalization after the 2023 peak, with terrorism-related deaths declining by 13% to 7,555 and incidents by 3% to 3,492. Yet, this apparent downturn conceals a widening crisis: the number of affected countries rose from 58 to 66, and the Sahel region now accounts for 51% of all terrorism deaths. Islamic State and its affiliates remain the most lethal network despite a 10% fall in attributed deaths, while Jamaat Nusrat Al-Islam wal Muslimeen (JNIM) has emerged as the deadliest actor in the Sahel. Beyond metrics, the review uncovers the convergence of state fragility, geopolitical rivalry, and the crime-terror nexus, where illicit economies such as artisanal mining and kidnapping sustain insurgency. It also highlights climate change as a potent threat multiplier and digital technologies as accelerants of radicalization. Integrating macrolevel economic cycle theory with micro-level threat models, the study forecasts a volatile decade ahead and emphasizes the need for anticipatory counterterrorism strategies.

title: On methodological incongruence in applying Generative AI in qualitative data analysis
affiliations: Monash University and Max-Planck Society

detail.title: On methodological incongruence in applying Generative AI in qualitative data analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no conflict of interests.
declarations.funderStatement: We have received no funding for this study.

detail.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative AI (GenAI) into qualitative research has created a "methodological crossroads." This article argues that current trends, specifically the attempt to automate qualitative coding with Large Language Models (LLMs), result in methodological incongruence. Drawing on Clarke et al. (2025), we identify how forcing probabilistic models to perform deterministic coding tasks creates a gap between qualitative values (depth, context, reflexivity) and actual practices (fragmentation, surface-level extraction). We propose that coding is a "skeuomorphic" workaround for human cognitive limits that is unnecessary for AI. To resolve this, we introduce a set of methodological tenets based on nonpositivist qualitative research and three frameworks including Conversational Analysis with AI (CA AI), Query Based Analysis (QBA) and Narrative-Interpretive Thematic Analysis (NITA). We advocate for a shift from "partitioning data" to "holistic querying", positioning the AI as an assistant and the researcher as the interpreter. Finally, we argue for an epistemological shift from "solitary" to "relational" meaning-making, demonstrating how this approach remains congruent with the principles of reflexive qualitative research.

title: Mapping Theoretical Perspectives for Requisite Resilience
affiliations: University of Strasbourg, University of Applied Sciences Kehl and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Mapping Theoretical Perspectives for Requisite Resilience
detail.abstract: In increasingly turbulent environments, organizations must go beyond generic robustness and develop Requisite Resilience, the capacity to align internal variety with environmental variety to sustain core functions during crises. This study situates Requisite Resilience within organizational theory and strategic management, assessing how major theories of the firm contribute to its development. The analysis groups these perspectives into foundational/diagnostic theories, which clarify environmental, structural and institutional constraints and correspond to passive resilience frameworks, and enabling/capabilitybuilding theories, which emphasize managerial agency, resource orchestration and adaptive learning, corresponding to active resilience frameworks. Findings indicate that while foundational perspectives offer essential diagnostics, they are insufficient on their own to foster Requisite Resilience. A composite configuration provides the strongest fit: coevolutionary views offer an integrative backbone, dynamic capabilities and organizational learning enhance sensing, seizing and acting, and resource dependence theory informs the design of permeable boundaries.

title: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using a Reformer-Based Model with Multi-Scale Dynamic Temporal Convolution and Enhanced Invertible Instance Normalization
affiliations: Wuhan Polytechnic University, Wuhan Polytechnic University, , , Wuhan Polytechnic University and

detail.title: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using a Reformer-Based Model with Multi-Scale Dynamic Temporal Convolution and Enhanced Invertible Instance Normalization
detail.abstract: Short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting plays a pivotal role in the operation of PV power systems and the management of the electrical grid.Accurate PV power prediction provides essential data support for optimizing grid operations. This study proposes a deep learning algorithm named TCR-Reformer (Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using a Reformer-Based Model with Multi-Scale Dynamic Temporal Convolution and Enhanced Invertible Instance Normalization) to address the challenges of data dis-tribution shift and multi-scale coupling of temporal features in PV powerforecasting.The algorithm is based on the Reformer architecture and in-corporates an enhanced invertible instance normalization mechanism (Ad-vReVin) and a Multi-Scale Dynamic Temporal Convolutional Network (MS-DTCN).These integrations are designed to enhance the model’s ability to handle non-stationary time series and improve its temporal modeling within local receptive fields,while preserving the Reformer’s inherent efficiency in processing long sequences.To validate the practical applicability of the pro-posed method in PV power generation scenarios,we evaluated its performance using real-world data from multiple PV power stations in Guizhou Province,provided by Guizhou Qianyuan Power Co., Ltd.,spanning from October 2022 to January 2024.The results show that,under the industry evaluation stan-dards of the China Southern Power Grid,the proposed method achieved pre-diction accuracies of 75.67% and 73.60%.Compared to classic models such as Transformer, Informer, Autoformer, iTransformer, and Reformer,our method improved prediction accuracy by 1-3% and reduced the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by approximately 15%.The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can deliver high prediction accuracy in photovoltaic power systems.

title: Materials constraints for long-term photovoltaic sustainability: renewal dynamics highlight critical mining and recycling needs
affiliations: Université Paris Cité, Université Paris Cité and Université Paris Cité

detail.title: Materials constraints for long-term photovoltaic sustainability: renewal dynamics highlight critical mining and recycling needs
detail.abstract: Energy transition scenarios anticipate a substantial increase in material demand driven by the large-scale deployment of low-carbon technologies, particularly photovoltaics. Existing assessments typically limit their time horizon to 2050, which aligns with political targets and allow identifying short-term supply risks, but remains insufficient for evaluating the long-term material requirements associated with technology replacement and sustained operation. We develop a dynamic stock–flow model to explore PV deployment trajectories until 2100, incorporating assumptions on material intensity reductions, module lifetimes, and both primary and secondary (recycled) material supply. Using IEA’s Net Zero Emissions scenario, we find that the material requirements for maintaining the global PV fleet could create significant pressure on several key resources after 2050. Copper emerges as the most critical material: under a business-as-usual supply scenario, PV demand could account for more than 50% of annual primary copper production by 2080. Comparable long-term constraints appear for silver and aluminium. These pressures arise beyond mid-century, underscoring the importance of extending assessment horizons for evaluating the sustainability of low-carbon technologies. The large number of PV modules reaching end-of-life after 2050 will create a significant secondary feedstock. With efficient recycling, this could delay material shortages by decades. Recycling 40% of end-of-life panel copper would reduce PV’s share of primary copper demand to around 30% in 2080. Overall, our results indicate that long-term material requirements for sustaining PV may impose supply pressures comparable to, or exceeding, those associated with initial deployment, highlighting the need for coordinated strategies on material efficiency, recycling, and long-term resource planning.

detail.abstract:
The Doctrine of Anchored Decentralization presents the first integrated constitutional and statutory framework capable of reconciling decentralized digital architectures with the structural logic of the United States legal order. As the second installment in The Republic’s Conscience series, this work extends foundational principles of constitutional accountability into digital-asset governance, administrative demarcation, and federal statutory coherence.

The Doctrine introduces an architecture-based commodity–security classification regime grounded in verifiable system behavior rather than self-described decentralization. Synthesizing Howey, Reves, Forman, Marbury, and post-Chevron jurisprudence, it provides Congress, courts, and regulators with a methodologically rigorous, adjudicable standard capable of surviving textualist review.

The analysis rejects the notion that blockchain systems may operate as “stateless” economic entities while relying on U.S. markets and infrastructure. Anchored in Article I’s monetary and commercial powers, the appropriations constraints of Article I, § 9, and the Due Process Clauses, the Doctrine demonstrates that most digital systems function within a constitutional vacuum, performing economic coordination without satisfying the representational prerequisites of the Republic’s Chain of Consent—the principle that legitimate economic power must be traceable to accountable authority.

At the engineering level, the work reframes decentralization as a cryptographic lineage originating with Haber and Stornetta’s timestamping architecture, establishing that Bitcoin’s defining contribution is distributed verification—not monetary creation. This distinction reveals why most digital tokens cannot qualify as commodities under the Commodity Exchange Act unless they demonstrate origin accountability, managerial neutrality, and architectural immutability.

The Doctrine identifies structural defects in contemporary legislative approaches, including H.R. 3633, which misapply commodity theory and institutionalize anonymity architectures that undermine due process and enforcement integrity. In response, the work introduces the Anchored Decentralization Test—the first system-level doctrine allowing classification based on verifiable architecture rather than narrative.

It further advances Autonomous Commodity Primitives (ACPs), a sovereign-grade infrastructure class designed as immutable cryptographic attestations of real sovereign reserve assets, enabling constitutionally compliant Asset-Backed Digital Currency (ABDC) systems without speculative behavior.

To reconcile privacy with constitutional accountability, the Doctrine integrates Zero-Knowledge Proofs and non-custodial audit layers, restoring lawful traceability without creating surveillance architecture.

The work concludes that decentralization without accountability constitutes a structural form of constitutional evasion—an economic sphere operating beyond representation. By restoring constitutional anchoring to distributed systems, the Doctrine reaffirms the Republic’s foundational principle: economic power is legitimate only when traceable to the people from whom the Constitution draws all authority.

title: Investment Grants: Curse Or Blessing for Employment?
affiliations: Halle Institute for Economic Research

detail.title: Investment Grants: Curse Or Blessing for Employment?
detail.abstract: In this study, establishment-level employment effects of investment grants in Germany are estimated. In addition to the quantitative effects, I provide empirical evidence of funding effects on different aspects of employment quality (earnings, qualifications, and job security) for the period 2004 to 2020. The database combines project-level treatment data, establishment-level information on firm characteristics and employee structure, and regional information at the district-level. For the estimations, I combine the difference-indifferences approach of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) with ties matching at the cohort level. The estimations yield positive effects on the number of employees, but point to contradicting effects of investment grants on different aspects of employment quality.

title: Market Opportunity for Indian Private Funds: A Prospect Generator Model for Supporting India's Renewable Energy Transition through Overseas Mineral Projects
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Shillong

detail.title: Market Opportunity for Indian Private Funds: A Prospect Generator Model for Supporting India's Renewable Energy Transition through Overseas Mineral Projects
detail.abstract: The global mining landscape is undergoing significant transformation, driven by rising demand for critical minerals essential to renewable energy technologies. Major mining companies are increasingly seeking early-stage projects abroad to secure strategic resources, creating favourable market conditions for investors and project developers. This paper explores the applicability of the Prospect Generator model for Indian private firms aiming to participate in overseas mineral projects that support India's renewable energy transition. The model involves acquiring or identifying underexplored mineral prospects, enhancing their value through technical validation and early-stage exploration, and monetizing them through joint ventures, farm-outs, or sales to larger mining companies or public sector undertakings (PSUs). By leveraging a portfolio-based approach, optionality, and current market demand, Indian firms can efficiently capture value while managing operational and financial risks. The study discusses mechanisms of value creation, governance considerations, and risk management strategies, demonstrating that the Prospect Generator model offers an asset-light and strategically aligned pathway for Indian private firms to contribute to the country's renewable energy objectives.

title: A Probabilistic Evaluation of the Evolution of Capital Costs and their Reduction Potential for New Nuclear Power Plants
affiliations: Government of the United States of America - Idaho National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Idaho National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Idaho National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Idaho National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Idaho National Laboratory and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

detail.title: A Probabilistic Evaluation of the Evolution of Capital Costs and their Reduction Potential for New Nuclear Power Plants
detail.abstract: SUMMARYThis study presents a probabilistic evaluation of capital cost and construction schedule overruns and reduction potentials for building a series of new nuclear power plants in the United States. High capital costs for first-of-a-kind (FOAK) projects present a significant barrier to investments and creates a “first-mover” problem that can best be resolved through committed orderbook of several plants that are built sequentially. The study in this paper models the evolution of cost and construction duration in such orderbooks from the first to the last plant as a function of "levers" such as order book size, interest rates, design completion level before construction, etc. Results show that the first plant, which is assumed to be “first-of-a-kind”, is prone to significant cost and schedule overruns (median cost overrun of around 130%), while the last plant benefits from a gradual reduction in overruns as well as learning-based efficiencies that result in cost and schedule reductions (median cost reduction of around 30%).The study also identifies specific project characteristics of “levers” that determine overruns. For example, projects with FOAK capital cost overruns under 25% typically have at least five firm orders, 55% of their design completed before construction begins, a high level of design maturity, moderate to high proficiency in architecture/engineering and supply chain quality, a high proficiency in nuclear plant construction, and utilize modular civil construction. With the United States gearing up to significantly increase nuclear capacity, this study intends to provide insights into project planning aspects that enable the most economical pathways to achieve this scale up. The framework can be customized to any plant technology and has the potential to help policymakers, utilities, and stakeholders to make informed decisions by providing a detailed, customizable approach to cost estimation and reduction strategies.

title: Navigating the Paradox: A Contingent Volatility Model of Performance Management for Workforce Resilience and Striving

detail.title: Navigating the Paradox: A Contingent Volatility Model of Performance Management for Workforce Resilience and Striving
detail.abstract: This paper aims to resolve the theoretical stalemate in performance management by introducing a paradox-informed model that addresses the core tension between stability and adaptation. It moves beyond systems-level debate to explain the psychological capacities required for this paradox. Introducing the novel "contingent volatility" principle, the paper integrates Paradox Theory with Self-Determination Theory to build a multi-level model. It redefines workforce resilience and employee striving as symbiotic outcomes of psychological need satisfaction. A practical blueprint details how strategic, managerial, and individual practices can simultaneously provide stability and support adaptation. This conceptual contribution requires future testing and implementation challenges, necessitating careful cultural adaptation. It provides leaders a blueprint for human-centric frameworks and guides managers as "paradox navigators," offering a specific logic for building context-sensitive, agile systems that transcend the rigidity-chaos dichotomy. As a conceptual theory-building paper, it presents a detailed theoretical model and a set of testable propositions to guide future empirical research.

title: Notes on Sustainability, Corporate responsibility (CSR), Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and B3's
affiliations: Pontifical Catholic University of Sao Paolo (PUCSP)

detail.title: Notes on Sustainability, Corporate responsibility (CSR), Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and B3's

publicationDetails.detailsText: Brazilian Journal of Development, Vol. 11, No. 5, Pp. 1-22

detail.abstract: This article dives into how the SDGs are being integrated into corporate practices, with a focus on Brazil's B3 Corporate Sustainability Index (ISE). It evaluates how committed companies are to sustainable practices and how well they align with the SDGs. The article starts with a literature review, exploring key concepts like sustainability, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and the Triple Bottom Line (TBL).The study also examines the ISE B3 as a tool for measuring the sustainability performance of companies listed on the Brazilian stock exchange, emphasizing the importance of transparency and accountability. The ISE B3 stands out as a valuable tool for assessing companies' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, pushing them toward sustainable practices and attracting socially conscious investors. However, integrating the SDGs into corporate strategies isn't without challenges. Issues like unclear metrics and the need for better collaboration between sectors remain significant hurdles. The article concludes that combining the SDGs with the ISE B3 can bring real benefits for companies, including better visibility, improved reputations, and higher profitability. But more research is needed to figure out how to make these frameworks work effectively, especially in local contexts. Ultimately, adopting sustainable practices shouldn't be seen as just an ethical duty-it's a smart strategy for long-term success in a world where consumers and investors increasingly care about the environment and social responsibility.

title: Resilience Oriented Coupled Scheduling of Data-Energy Flow in Internet Data Center-Integrated Energy Systems
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Resilience Oriented Coupled Scheduling of Data-Energy Flow in Internet Data Center-Integrated Energy Systems
detail.abstract: In recent years, the frequent occurrence of disasters has posed significant challenges to the resilience of Internet data center-integrated energy systems (IDC-IES). In this regard, a coupled scheduling strategy is proposed to enhance the resilience of IDC-IES under disasters. Initially, a multi-dimensional resilience assessment metric is constructed for the IDC-IES based on the dynamic Bayesian network (DBN). Incorporating both an energy consumption model and a cross-seasonal heat storage (CSHS) model for IDCs, an IDC-IES model is established with a coordinated mechanism of data-energy flow. The proposed strategy aims to minimize the cost of workload loss and workload scheduling, the cost of electric and thermal load loss in IDC-IES as well as the cost of repair crews’ scheduling. Furthermore, a quantum-enhanced multi-objective gray wolf optimization (QMOGWO) algorithm is designed to solve the proposed strategy. Finally, case studies are conducted to demonstrate that the integration of dynamic workload scheduling and CSHS effectively enhances the resilience of the IDC-IES, significantly improving the ability to withstand disasters.

title: Who Wins in the Matrix? A Theory of Credit Attribution in Status Economies Working Paper -Version 1.0

detail.title: Who Wins in the Matrix? A Theory of Credit Attribution in Status Economies Working Paper -Version 1.0
detail.abstract:
Why do technically excellent employees fail to receive credit commensurate with their contributions? This paper proposes a causal model of credit attribution: μ = f(θ, ε, A, D, S, B, η), where recognized credit (μ) is a function of production skill (θ), agent actions influencing own credit (ε), third-party advocacy (A), appropriation by others (D), system design (S), evaluator bias (B), and noise (η). While prior research has examined individual factors, no existing framework integrates them into a unified causal structure. This paper focuses specifically on ε—the agent-controlled portion of credit attribution—while situating it within the complete model. We decompose ε into five action categories (visibility, narrative, coalition, defense, signal management) and distinguish between ethical and unethical actions within each. An agent-based simulation validates the framework's core prediction: controlling for θ, variance in ε explains substantial variance in advancement outcomes.
The framework extends tournament theory by formalizing credit assignment as multiply determined rather than structurally given, and provides practitioners with actionable guidance on the factors within their control. For organizations, it establishes that reducing 'politics' requires investment in attribution infrastructure, not cultural exhortation.

title: Dual-agent System Integrating Multi-head Attention Mechanisms Solves Multi-objective Dynamic Flexible Job Scheduling Shop Problem
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Dual-agent System Integrating Multi-head Attention Mechanisms Solves Multi-objective Dynamic Flexible Job Scheduling Shop Problem
detail.abstract: The dynamic flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP) demands improved scheduling efficiency, shortened production cycles, and balanced machining status of workshop machines. To address this, a dual-agent proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm integrating graph neural networks (GNN) and multi-head attention mechanisms, with the objectives of minimizing the maximum makespan, reducing machine idle rate, and enhancing machine load balancing rate is proposed. The DFJSP is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) where the state space is constructed in the form of the heterogeneous graph. It defines the state and action spaces of the workpiece and machine, designs a novel multi-objective reward function to minimize completion time, reduce machine idle rate, and improve machine load balancing rate, and establishes a dynamic hierarchical scheduling framework with two-stage collaborative processing of workpiece selection and machine allocation. A novel multi-objective reward function is designed, and a dynamic hierarchical scheduling framework featuring two-stage collaborative processing—job selection and machine assignment—is established. The multi-head attention mechanism is introduced to strengthen the capability of capturing correlation features between job states and machine states, thereby improving the generalization performance of the policy and robustness against dynamic disturbances. Ablation experiments demonstrate that the proposed multi-head attention mechanism, dual-agent approach, and novel advantage estimation all improve the algorithm's performance. Comparative experiments show that the proposed algorithm has significant advantages in terms of solution quality and generalization performance.

title: Level of Employees' Satisfaction towards Flexible Work Arrangement in a Selected Local Government in Region V
affiliations: World Citi Colleges, World Citi Colleges, World Citi Colleges, World City Colleges Quezon City Graduate Department and World Citi Colleges

detail.title: Level of Employees' Satisfaction towards Flexible Work Arrangement in a Selected Local Government in Region V
detail.abstract: This study, entitled "Level of Employees' Satisfaction Towards Flexible Work Arrangement in a Selected Local Government in Region V," examined the influence of Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) on employee satisfaction in a local government setting. It aimed to assess satisfaction in terms of work-life balance, productivity and performance, communication and collaboration, and organizational support. A descriptive-correlational design was employed with 150 respondents from various departments of the selected Local Government Unit (LGU) in Region V. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using frequency distribution, weighted mean, and correlation analysis through SPSS Version 27. Findings revealed that employees generally agreed that FWAs contribute positively to their satisfaction, particularly in maintaining work-life balance (WM = 3.36) and improving productivity (WM = 3.34). The overall weighted mean of 3.33 indicated a moderate to high level of satisfaction and effective implementation of flexible work policies. Results also showed a significant positive relationship between the implementation of FWAs and employee satisfaction, suggesting that flexibility enhances morale and organizational commitment. The study concludes that flexible work arrangements promote employee well-being and efficiency in local government institutions. It recommends the establishment of clear policies, improved communication systems, and capacity-building initiatives to ensure consistent and sustainable implementation.

title: PBCAE: A Unified Process-Based Cognitive Architecture for Modeling and Engineering Human and Hybrid Cognition

detail.title: PBCAE: A Unified Process-Based Cognitive Architecture for Modeling and Engineering Human and Hybrid Cognition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or organizational conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This manuscript presents a conceptual and theoretical framework. No human subjects, personal data, or clinical interventions were involved; therefore ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: The work was conducted during the author’s PhD research at KU Leuven; however, no specific funding was allocated for this manuscript.

detail.abstract:
Cognition is typically described through static representations, symbolic states, or loosely defined mental constructs. This paper introduces PBCAE (Process-Based Cognitive Architecture & Engineering), a unified framework that reconceptualizes cognition as an executable process system grounded in process ontology, distributed cognition, and formal modeling languages such as BPMN and Petri Nets. PBCAE models cognitive episodes – perception, reasoning, metacognition, and self-regulation – as dynamic workflows composed of states, transitions, control flows, branching structures, and parallel processes.

The architecture provides (a) a formal ontology of cognitive processes, (b) an executable modeling paradigm for representing human thought, and (c) an engineering framework for designing, simulating, and improving cognitive workflows.

PBCAE further extends to hybrid human-AI cognition, enabling precise modeling of the structural asymmetry between human sequential reasoning and transformer-based AI’s parallel inference. This integration forms the basis for Distributed Cognition Loop (DCL) mechanisms, in which human and AI agents coordinate through shared process representations.

The paper outlines the theoretical foundations of PBCAE, defines its cognitive layers (L1-L6), demonstrates its formal modeling principles, and presents applications across knowledge work, cognitive education, behavioral game theory, psychotherapy, and enterprise architecture.

PBCAE provides a foundation for a new generation of cognitive systems research and hybrid intelligence engineering, treating cognition not as an abstract construct but as an executable, analyzable, and improvable process architecture.

title: Hierarchical Simulation–Optimization Framework for Aquifer Storage and Recovery Systems
affiliations: Sultan Qaboos University, University of Kent - Kent Business School, , Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Tarbiat Modares University, Tarbiat Modares University, Tarbiat Modares University and University of Luxembourg

detail.title: Hierarchical Simulation–Optimization Framework for Aquifer Storage and Recovery Systems
detail.abstract: This study presents a hierarchical simulation–optimization framework for designing Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) systems in a coastal karst aquifer in northeast Qatar. A three-dimensional, variable-density SEAWAT model (embedded directly without surrogates) is coupled to a customized genetic algorithm that adds wells sequentially only when they deliver positive marginal value. The optimization maximizes an extended net present value (NPV) that accounts for revenues from recovered water, capital and operating costs, emergency-supply cost avoidance, and deferred desalination capacity, while propagating recharge uncertainty via Monte Carlo sampling within the fitness evaluations. Feasibility is enforced through graded penalties on water-quality thresholds, well spacing, and model-domain/layer constraints, and convergence is accelerated through pre-run screening and parallel evaluations. Applied to Qatar’s northeast coastal aquifer, the framework selects three well-field zones aligned with the national water-transfer corridor; attempts to add a fourth zone decrease value due to upconing/salinization penalties. Across 100 Monte Carlo re-evaluations, the recommended layout yields an expected NPV of ≈ USD 2.08 billion (σ ≈ 0.093 billion), maintains hydraulic heads above a 5 m safety threshold, and limits salinity increases—largest at the coast-proximal zone but within standards. Spatial impacts remain localized, with no broad inland migration of the coastal saline wedge. The approach provides a scalable, physically faithful pathway to stage ASR infrastructure under uncertainty, supporting economically viable and operationally robust water-security planning in arid coastal settings.

title: Integrated Three-Layer Framework for Planning the Operation of Hydrogen Fuel-Cell Buses
affiliations: National Penghu University of Science and Technology, National Dong Hwa University and National Dong Hwa University

detail.title: Integrated Three-Layer Framework for Planning the Operation of Hydrogen Fuel-Cell Buses
detail.abstract: This study developed an integrated, cross-layer optimization framework for planning hydrogen fuel cell bus (FCB) operations and infrastructure; this study tested the framework on Tainan City’s 14-depot, 121-route network. The 10-year total cost, including costs related to vehicles, hydrogen production, storage, transport, and electricity, was divided into three categories: (i) timetable integration and minimum fleet sizing; (ii) supply chain design for localized and centralized production, depot pairing, and truck scheduling; and (iii) joint sizing of production and storage equipment under time-of-use tariffs. Four decision subvectors, namely departure station, carrier station, local production ratios, and daytime electrolysis hours, were encoded into a single chromosome. Artificial bee colony and a genetic algorithm (GA) were integrated with single-, two-, and three-layer search strategies. The proposed three-layer workflow sequentially involves fixing departure depots, optimizing the hydrogen production and distribution layout, and fine-tuning daytime production hours. With the GA, the three-layer strategy yielded the lowest 10-year cost of US $246.22 million, which was 9.4% and 0.5% lower than those obtained using the single- and two-layer approaches, respectively. The optimum schedule requires 271 buses, 23 production plants, 10 storage stations, and 5 tube trailers, eliminating 22 buses and 13 plants compared with a fully centralized baseline. The results indicate that hierarchical optimization markedly improves convergence and cost efficiency by balancing economies of scale in hydrogen production with the operational flexibility of decentralized dispatch. Future research should incorporate stochastic energy prices, real-time rescheduling, and multiobjective emission metrics to enhance the robustness and sustainability   of FCB systems.

title: Configurational Pathways to Smart City AI Adoption: Evidence from Local Governments in Australia, the US, Spain, Hong Kong, and Saudi Arabia
affiliations: Queensland University of Technology, Queensland University of Technology, Queensland University of Technology, Queensland University of Technology, Queensland University of Technology, Arizona State University (ASU) and University of Salamanca

detail.title: Configurational Pathways to Smart City AI Adoption: Evidence from Local Governments in Australia, the US, Spain, Hong Kong, and Saudi Arabia
detail.abstract: Despite growing policy attention and technological advances, AI adoption in smart city governance remains uneven. While prior research has explored individual adoption drivers, few studies examine how multiple factors interact to enable or constrain implementation. Drawing on the technology–community–policy framework, this study uses fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to explore configurational pathways to AI-enabled smart city adoption across eleven local governments in Australia, the US, Spain, Hong Kong, and Saudi Arabia. Results reveal three equifinal pathways leading to comparable adoption outcomes. The technology-driven pathway shows that strong smart city infrastructure and data capability can offset limited regulatory readiness. The balanced pathway combines technological readiness, policy awareness, and community orientation to support adoption holistically. The policy-driven pathway highlights that strong institutional mandates can compensate for weaker technical capacity. Across all configurations, perceived implementation constraints emerge as a core enabler, indicating that recognizing challenges can prompt proactive adoption strategies. These findings demonstrate substitutability between technological and policy dimensions, offering strategic flexibility for municipalities with varying resources. This study advances configurational thinking in smart city research and public sector innovation, providing actionable guidance for designing context-sensitive, resource-appropriate AI governance strategies in local governments.

title: Carbon Behavior Is Not Human Nature: A Structural Theory of Emission and Infrastructure Parity

detail.title: Carbon Behavior Is Not Human Nature: A Structural Theory of Emission and Infrastructure Parity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal conflicts of interest. This work is an independent conceptual and theoretical contribution developed by the author without external influence.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This work does not involve human participants, experiments, or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work. This research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The prevailing narrative in climate policy assumes carbon emissions are driven primarily by individual behavior, cultural choices, or developmental stage. This paper challenges that assumption. Emissions are not expressions of human nature — they are outcomes of infrastructure. Drawing from cross-contextual behavioral evidence across high-income and low-income environments, we introduce a new distinction in climate theory: Compulsory Carbon (infrastructure-imposed emissions) vs. Discretionary Carbon (preference-based emissions) We argue that the majority of global emissions — particularly in emerging regions — arise from infrastructural necessity, not voluntary consumption. Consequently, mitigating emissions requires a structural engineering paradigm, not moral persuasion. Climate justice must evolve from redistribution rhetoric to infrastructure parity. This reframing shifts climate economics from behavioral theory to infrastructure determinism, presenting emissions as a function of systemic provision rather than personal preference.

title: EvoMarkets: An Agent-Based Simulation of Strategy, Latency, and Tail Risk in a High-Fidelity Limit Order Book
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: EvoMarkets: An Agent-Based Simulation of Strategy, Latency, and Tail Risk in a High-Fidelity Limit Order Book
detail.abstract: This paper introduces EvoMarkets, an agent-based market simulator that integrates game-theoretic reasoning with high-frequency limit order book (LOB) dynamics. Strategies from the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma are reinterpreted as trading behaviors: cooperation corresponds to liquidity provision through passive limit orders, while defection represents aggressive liquidity consumption via market orders. I built a hybrid C++/Python engine and evaluated ten heterogeneous agents across static and evolutionary experiments. In a round-robin tournament, adaptive learners such as the ThompsonAgent consistently achieved the highest profit and lowest tail risk (CVaR), while purely aggressive and random agents, like AlwaysDefect and RandomAgent, suffered catastrophic drawdowns. However, under evolutionary pressure, **no single strategy dominated**: the population converged into a stable, mixed equilibrium of cooperative and retaliatory types, with aggressive and random strategies going extinct. **Notably, strategies that attempted moral reciprocity-like Tit-for-Tat-failed because i structured retaliation as expensive, illustrating how microstructural friction transforms classical game-theory outcomes. ** These results show that market stability and liquidity emerge from the evolutionary persistence of adaptive restraint, highlighting the deep connection between market physics, learning, and systemic resilience.
