detail.abstract: Purpose This study addresses the persistent fragmentation of sustainability education by proposing the EDGES-AI Compass, an integrated framework that unites ethical, digital, green, and AI-enabled learning into a coherent competency-oriented model for higher education aligned with global sustainability goals. Design/methodology/approach A PRISMA-aligned systematic literature review of 91 Q1–Q2 studies (2020–2025) registered on the Open Science Framework informed the development of the framework through thematic coding, cross-domain synthesis, and validation via theoretical mapping and competency alignment. Findings Evidence shows increasing convergence among ethical reasoning, digital fluency, ecological literacy, and responsible AI use in higher education. The EDGES AI Compass organizes this convergence into four orientations and four layers: competencies, pedagogy, assessment, and institutional practice. These layers are supported by recurring strategies that combine experiential learning, transformative approaches, and technology-enhanced learning, grounded in systems thinking. Originality/value This study presents an empirically grounded model that integrates established and emerging pedagogies within a single structure for sustainability education, illustrating how ethically governed intelligent technologies can strengthen human judgment and advance system-level transformation in higher education. Practical implications The framework provides educators and universities with a structured guide for curriculum redesign, competency mapping, assessment of transformative outcomes, and governance mechanisms for institution-wide adoption aligned with Education for Sustainable Development and SDG 4.7.

title: Identity as Constraint Geometry: A Unified Framework for Structural, Episodic, and Generative Identity
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: Identity as Constraint Geometry: A Unified Framework for Structural, Episodic, and Generative Identity
detail.abstract:
Identity is one of the most widely used yet least coherently defined concepts across philosophy,
biology, artificial intelligence, mathematics, and institutional theory. Existing accounts
depend on domain-specific assumptions—substance, causality, continuity, memory, or narrative
structure—that do not generalize across systems or scales. This work develops a unified,
substrate-agnostic theory of identity grounded in constraint geometry rather than metaphysics.
Identity is defined as a region of invariance within a possibility field determined by a system’s
structural constraints (𝐶𝑠), dynamical constraints (𝐶𝑑), and an interpretive frame (IF) selecting
invariants and evaluation scales (Δ𝑡). This formulation yields three canonical regimes:
point identity (instantaneous coherence), field identity (episodic coherence), and flow identity
(generative persistence).
Two existing frameworks nest naturally within this geometry. PatternSense characterizes
flow identity through the invariance of a generative kernel within a stability basin, offering a
diachronic account applicable to organisms, institutions, and long-range computational processes.
The Operational Definition of Episodic Identity (ODEI) specifies conditions under
which artificial systems exhibit identity within individual runs, capturing short-timescale coherence
through integration spikes, sustained internal state, internal revision dynamics, and
task-coupled resource intensification.
The resulting theory resolves long-standing confusions surrounding personal identity, biological
individuality, system coherence, and computational unity. It distinguishes ontic identity
(constraint satisfaction) from operational identity (thresholded use), accommodates latent and
uninstantiated identities, and explains identity drift, bifurcation, fusion, and extinction in geometric
terms. The framework offers a shared vocabulary for disciplines that have previously
spoken past one another, and provides a principled foundation for analyzing identity in artificial
systems without recourse to behavioral projection or anthropomorphic inference.

title: Is Political Skill Always Beneficial? Why and When Politically Skilled Employees Become Targets of Coworker Social Undermining
affiliations: Tulane University

detail.title: Is Political Skill Always Beneficial? Why and When Politically Skilled Employees Become Targets of Coworker Social Undermining

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Approved by Tulane University IRB
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported in part by the Lepage Faculty Fellowship awarded to me, by A.B. Freeman School of Business, Tulane University.

detail.abstract: The benefits of political skill at work have been extensively documented and highlighted. Existing research also reports unexpectedly equivocal and even positive relationships between employee political skill and coworker social undermining, suggesting that politically skilled employees can become targets of coworker social undermining. However, there is a lack of research explaining why and when employee political skill can lead to coworker social undermining. This research, drawing from social rank theory and the theory of rivalry, offers a novel lens to answer these questions. Specifically, I theorize that employee political skill evokes coworker social undermining by affecting coworker perception of status threat, particularly when the coworker views the focal politically skilled employee as a personal rival. Findings from four studies—one correlational two-wave study and three experiments—provide support for these predictions. Further, non-rival competition and interpersonal disliking as alternative potential explanations to the hypothesized moderating effects of rivalry were ruled out. This study provides a theory-driven explanation of an unintended consequence of employee political skill and offers a more balanced understanding of the effects of political skill at work. Theoretical and future research implications are discussed.

title: Border Villages as Strategic Nodes: Enhancing Cross-Border Vigilance and Security Development Along the Indian Border with China
affiliations: and CSJM University

detail.title: Border Villages as Strategic Nodes: Enhancing Cross-Border Vigilance and Security Development Along the Indian Border with China
detail.abstract: The Line of Actual Control (LAC) has been tense recently, with the fiercest border conflict since 1962 at Galwan Valley in 2020. Despite extensive talks, trust is absent on both sides. Apart from infrastructural development and military buildup, new methods of increasing vigilance are being used by both, which include building Xiaokang or 'well-off villages' from the Chinese side and rehabilitating border villages by the Indian side. Indian border villages have historically held strategic importance but have become depopulated due to limited opportunities, leaving them as 'ghost villages.' India is working to support these villages and counter Chinese tactics to maintain territorial integrity. India can improve security and bilateral cooperation by leveraging the strategic and socioeconomic potential of these villages. This paper examines the importance of border villages as hubs for cross-border surveillance and security measures amid geopolitical tensions, border conflicts, and broader security concerns. It aims to understand how these villages can promote peace, prosperity, and resilience in the Indo-China border region and provide policy recommendations for their development, thereby maintaining peace in contested border areas.

title: Cumulative (dis)advantage and gender in working-class trajectories in Buenos Aires
affiliations: Universidad de Buenos Aires

detail.title: Cumulative (dis)advantage and gender in working-class trajectories in Buenos Aires
detail.abstract: This article deals with processes of cumulative advantage and disadvantage in trajectories of social mobility from a gender perspective. In order to investigate how working-class trajectories in the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area are shaped by gender in terms of the accumulation of (dis)advantage, we carried out biographical interviews with individuals from different social backgrounds within the working class. It was found that families with more stable situations were able to marshal resources in a way that made spirals of cumulative advantage more likely. Within this group, some men were able to take full advantage, while more often faced obstacles.

title: Suppression of Mathematical Rigor: Cargo Cult Science
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: Suppression of Mathematical Rigor: Cargo Cult Science
detail.abstract: On November 21, 2025, Preprints.org declined to announce a mathematical proof demonstrating that impedance matching theory contains fundamental logical errors when material characteristic impedance matches free-space impedance. The rejection provided no substantive reason-only a vague reference to "guidelines." This case exemplifies how even platforms ostensibly designed for unrestricted knowledge sharing have adopted gatekeeping mechanisms that suppress paradigmchallenging theoretical work. We analyze why this rejection is indefensible from both scientific and epistemological perspectives: (1) the manuscript presents rigorous mathematical proof, not speculation; (2) challenging established theories is precisely what preprint platforms should enable; (3) no "guideline violation" exists that would justify suppression of logically rigorous work; (4) the rejection represents institutional fear of paradigm challenge disguised as procedural enforcement. We argue that acceptance of such gatekeeping on platforms explicitly designed to circumvent journal gatekeeping represents a catastrophic failure of the preprint system's stated purpose. The case demonstrates that suppression of paradigm-challenging work has become institutionalized across the entire academic publishing ecosystem-from top-tier journals to alternative platforms. This analysis serves as documentation of systemic institutional failure to accommodate rigorous theoretical innovation.

title: Setbacks Big and Small
affiliations: University of Georgia - Terry College of Business, Duke University - Department of Economics, University of Washington - Department of Finance and Business Economics and Duke University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Setbacks Big and Small
detail.abstract: We study the optimal incentive contract for a time-to-build project subject to both major and minor setbacks. Setbacks are flaws in the project, discovered (not caused) by the agent, and the size is privately observed by him. The agent can exploit this informational advantage to hide being behind schedule, generating persistent private information. We show that the optimal contract is governed by a family of "no-postponed-setback" constraints that imply a weakly higher likelihood of termination following larger reported setbacks. These constraints provide a straightforward organizing principle for the optimal contract and clarify how continuation utility is rationed across histories. Our analysis complements the all-or-nothing environment we studied in Setbacks, Shutdowns, and Overruns (Econometrica, 2024) and offers tractable tools for settings in which effort incentives interact with persistent private information.

title: Screening Precommitment, Candidate Quality, and Time-to-Hire: An Experimental Investigation
affiliations: ,  and University of Waterloo - School of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Screening Precommitment, Candidate Quality, and Time-to-Hire: An Experimental Investigation

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study received ethics approval at the relevant institutions.

detail.abstract: Personnel controls over screening job candidates play a central role in helping firms efficiently hire quality employees. Using an experiment, we examine a personnel control that requires managers to precommit to the number of candidates they will screen before making a hiring decision. We find that screening precommitment leads managers to hire higher-quality candidates but lengthens the time-to-hire, compared to a no precommitment approach. The trade-off between hiring speed and candidate quality is reflected in firm earnings, where in our setting, faster hiring under no precommitment yields higher earnings despite lower hire quality. These findings highlight the managerial tension between efficiency and effectiveness in hiring and show how precommitment influences whether managers adopt a maximizing or satisficing approach to decision-making in uncertain, time-sensitive hiring settings.

title: QUANTIVESTA™: A Quantitative and Prescriptive Financial Intelligence Framework for Supply-Chain Security, Logistics Optimization, and Consumer-Goods Protection

detail.title: QUANTIVESTA™: A Quantitative and Prescriptive Financial Intelligence Framework for Supply-Chain Security, Logistics Optimization, and Consumer-Goods Protection
detail.abstract: Global supply chains face escalating volatility driven by inflationary shocks, logistics bottlenecks, geopolitical risk, and supplier fragility. Traditional financial intelligence tools remain predominantly retrospective and siloed, lacking the predictive foresight and prescriptive capability required for modern supply-chain decision-making. This paper introduces QUANTIVESTA™, a novel quantitative and prescriptive financial intelligence framework that unifies predictive modeling, optimization science, operational risk analytics, and real-time anomaly detection. Built on five analytical pillars PREDICT, OPTIMIZE, SECURE, ANALYZE, and EVOLVE the framework offers an integrated architecture that directly links financial performance to operational behavior. We present the QUANTIVESTA™ Financial Intelligence Index (FII™), a new maturity metric for financial-operational ecosystems, and demonstrate the framework's conceptual value through scenario-based evaluations. Results show potential improvements including a 30% increase in forecast accuracy, 20% reduction in reactive spending, and 5-8% annual margin recovery. QUANTIVESTA™ represents an original contribution to financial intelligence and supply-chain analytics by advancing enterprise systems toward real-time, prescriptive, and continuously adaptive decision-making.

title: Foundations of Entrepreneurship and Intrapreneurship: Concepts, Differences, and Interlinkages with the Entrepreneurial Profile, with Contributions from Social Entrepreneurship and Organizational Innovation

detail.title: Foundations of Entrepreneurship and Intrapreneurship: Concepts, Differences, and Interlinkages with the Entrepreneurial Profile, with Contributions from Social Entrepreneurship and Organizational Innovation
detail.abstract: This paper clarifies the distinctions and interconnections between entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, and social entrepreneurship, integrating classical foundations and contemporary perspectives. It examines the competencies that define the entrepreneurial profile and highlights how innovation, opportunity recognition, and mission-driven action operate across individual, organizational, and societal levels. Drawing on contributions from Schumpeter, Cantillon, Dees, Filion, and recent research on social innovation, the paper proposes a conceptual structure linking entrepreneurial activity to organizational learning, sustainable development, and ecosystem dynamics. The study offers a consolidated theoretical basis for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers interested in entrepreneurial models that generate both economic and social value.

title: Securitising AI: routine exceptionality and digital governance in the Gulf
affiliations: Doha Institute for Graduate Studies

detail.title: Securitising AI: routine exceptionality and digital governance in the Gulf
detail.abstract: This article examines how Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states securitise artificial intelligence (AI) through discourses and infrastructures that fuse modernisation with regime resilience. Drawing on securitisation theory (Buzan et al., 1998; Balzacq, 2011) and critical security studies, it analyses national strategies, surveillance systems, and mega-event governance in Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. It argues that AI functions as both a legitimising narrative and a technology of control, embedding predictive policing and biometric surveillance within public-private assemblages. The study situates these developments within global AI politics, demonstrating how external chokepoints, ethical frameworks, and vendor ecosystems shape the Gulf's evolving security governance, leading to empirical effects such as the normalisation of exceptional measures in everyday administration.

detail.title: Exemption of Inbound Dividends from Non-Corporate Taxes under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive -Opinion Statement ECJ-TF 4/2025 on the Decision the CJEU of 1 August 2025 in Cases C-92/24 to C-94/24, Banca Mediolanum
detail.abstract: This is an Opinion Statement prepared by the CFE ECJ Task Force on the CJEU decision of 1 August 2025 in Cases C-92/24 to C-94/24, Banca Mediolanum. This judgment concerns the application of the exemption method under Art 4(1)(a) of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (PSD) to a non-corporation tax, specifically the Italian regional tax on production activities (IRAP). Deviating from Advocate General Kokott’s Opinion and her proposed analysis of tax comparability, the Court concluded, based on a textual, contextual, and teleological interpretation, that ratione materiae the exemption under Art 4(1)(a) PSD applies to any tax which includes qualified dividends in its tax base. This is irrespective of the fact that Art 2 of the PSD defines its ratione personae by reference to specifically listed domestic corporate taxes, of which the IRAP is not one.

title: Appeasement is Risky and Dangerous – It’s Time for Business Leaders to Stand Up!

detail.title: Appeasement is Risky and Dangerous – It’s Time for Business Leaders to Stand Up!
detail.abstract: This short essay focuses on the relationship between business and authoritarian threats in general, and those posed by the second Trump administration in particular. Kowtowing to authoritarian leaders seems like an expedient way to generate short-term profits but the case of Hungary shows that autocratic 'friends' turn against businesspeople who do not give them their unqualified loyalty. Remaining silent seems like a prudent way to reduce short-term risks, but this does nothing to slow down the erosion of democracy, reduce long-term risks, or stave off corruption and economic decline. The paper recommends actions and strategies that business leaders should take, and it reflects on the likely risks and costs of appeasement. It asks business leaders to consider whether it is worth sacrificing democracy for short-term profits and shareholder value -- do they want to be remembered as gravediggers of democracy?

detail.abstract: Why do two people with equivalent talent and work ethic end up in radically different economic positions? This white paper introduces a unified framework grounded in dynamical systems theory that explains socioeconomic mobility through attractor dynamics—where wealth and poverty function as stable basins separated by critical thresholds. We present principles from physics applied to human trajectories: basin geometry, separatrix navigation, bifurcation control, and leverage optimization. Combined with recursive cognitive refinement methodology, the framework reveals why conventional effort-based approaches fail and identifies strategic principles for basin crossing. Critically, we demonstrate that what popular advice calls compounding represents two fundamentally different phenomena: pre-separatrix accumulation (effort dissipating into friction) versus post-separatrix true compounding (autonomous positive feedback). This distinction explains why identical effort produces radically asymmetric outcomes. This conceptual overview establishes theoretical foundations while operational details remain proprietary.

title: Pricing along Multiple Dimensions: Evidence from Airlines
affiliations: University of Toronto and Operations Management Area, Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Pricing along Multiple Dimensions: Evidence from Airlines
detail.abstract: This paper examines firms that simultaneously practice two kinds of price discrimination. We first present data from the airline industry where firms price discriminate according to both quality and advance purchases. We show that in some markets, the quality markup increases as the travel date approaches but the opposite is true in others. Next, we present a model illustrating how the quality markup charged by a price discriminating firm can increase, decrease or remain unchanged as time elapses, depending on the distribution of consumer valuations across time. We then present survey data showing that the observed effect in airlines is driven by differences in the motivation and characteristics of travelers in each market, which reconciles the predictions of the model and the empirical results. Finally, we illustrate the potential revenue losses for firms that do not fully incorporate all available information about consumer heterogeneity in their pricing decisions.

title: Relational Behavior Analysis: A Proposed Framework for Identity-Level Reinforcement through Admiration

detail.title: Relational Behavior Analysis: A Proposed Framework for Identity-Level Reinforcement through Admiration
detail.abstract: Relational Behavior Analysis (RBA) is a proposed psychological framework that examines admiration as a form of identity-level reinforcement that supports emotional regulation, resilience, and self-coherence. Traditional reinforcement models focus on behavior change through external contingencies, leaving identity processes largely unaddressed. This paper introduces a functional mechanism in which admiration-defined as a relational signal affirming a person's inherent character-acts to stabilize identity during stress, reduce emotional reactivity, and prevent collapse. Drawing from behavior analysis, educational psychology, relational-cultural theory, and stress regulation literature, RBA outlines two core constructs: the Law of Sustained Love, which describes admiration as a sustaining relational force, and the Model of Blocked Becoming, which conceptualizes identity collapse when admiration is absent or inconsistent. A naturalistic case vignette illustrates the proposed mechanism in real time during acute stress. Methodological considerations, theoretical alignment, and implications for educational settings, mental health practice, gifted populations, and dyadic relationships are discussed. This work provides a foundation for future empirical testing of admiration as a measurable relational reinforcer and introduces identity-level reinforcement as an important construct for psychological science.

title: Institutional Costs, Distortions, and Firm Performance: Evidence from China's Statistical Threshold Adjustments on Above-Scale Industrial Firms
affiliations: Tianjin University, China University of Mining & Technology and Yangzhou University

detail.title: Institutional Costs, Distortions, and Firm Performance: Evidence from China's Statistical Threshold Adjustments on Above-Scale Industrial Firms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No
declarations.ethicsApproval: No
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of institutional costs on firm performance using the discontinuity implicit in China's statistical system. In China, industrial firms with revenues exceeding a certain threshold are classified as "above-scale" and face substantially stricter supervision. Exploiting a difference-indifferences design that combines this statistical discontinuity with the threshold adjustment in 2011, we find that industrial firms operating between the old and new thresholds experienced a significant improvement in performance, relative to their immediate above-scale counterparts. Diminished operational costs and enhanced allocative efficiency emerge as plausible mechanisms. Overall, reduced institutional costs mitigate distortions and foster economic vitality.

title: Two-Particle Quantum Interference in Corporate Payouts: A Longitudinal Case Study of Alphabet Inc. (2019-2024)

detail.title: Two-Particle Quantum Interference in Corporate Payouts: A Longitudinal Case Study of Alphabet Inc. (2019-2024)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Quantumist.AI, a financial technology platform that operationalizes the Quantum Capital Dynamics framework presented in this study. The author also retains commercial rights to the reference text, The Mechanics of Investment Banking. While the proprietary "Quantum Interference Index" (QII) algorithm is utilized for this analysis, the core methodology, data sets, and derivation scripts have been made open-source within this submission to ensure full reproducibility and mitigate potential bias. No external funding was received for this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study utilizes publicly available financial market data and corporate regulatory filings (SEC Forms 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K). It does not involve human subjects, survey participants, or private data. As such, Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval was not required.
