detail.abstract: This paper presents a foundational calibration of the Quantum Capital Dynamics framework using Alphabet Inc.'s 2024 payout initiation as a primary exemplar. We test whether the simultaneous announcement of a $70 billion buyback and a maiden dividend follows linear superposition (additive value) or quantum interference (non-linear amplification). Using a proprietary "Quantum Interference Index" (QII) model, we analyze event interactions across five key payout dates from 2019 to 2024. Results indicate a constructive interference phase (θ < 45°) during the 2024 dual-payout event, generating a 10.1% market capitalization surge-significantly exceeding the option-implied move of 4.8%. This non-linear response suggests that dividends and buybacks function as entangled state variables rather than independent transactions. While focused on a single high-magnitude issuer, this study serves as the initial installment of a broader longitudinal analysis (n=50) aimed at generalizing these interaction effects across the large-cap technology sector.

title: The 'DigitalWashing' of India's Public Welfare: Evidence from the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana

detail.title: The 'DigitalWashing' of India's Public Welfare: Evidence from the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author reports there are no competing interests to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The project was approved by the Research Ethics Office, King's College London (KCL Ethics Ref: LRS-18/19-9118).
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by Marie Skłodowska-Curie European Training Network titled ‘Global India’ (Grant Agreement 722446) funded by the European Commission’s Horizon 2020 programme.

detail.abstract: The narrative about India's successful transformation of public welfare governance via the biometrics-linked digital identifier Aadhaar and associated digital public infrastructure (DPI) dominates mainstream policy discourse. This is despite local administrators continuing to encounter systemic inefficiencies and citizens facing inconvenience and exclusion. Challenging the dominant narrative, this article evaluates the digital innovations for public welfare through the lived experiences of citizens and local administrators. It draws on a multisited ethnographic study of the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana-a maternity cash entitlement, conducted in one of India's most impoverished states, Jharkhand. It proposes the idea of 'digitalwashing', a concept coined to describe the tendency to equate using digital tools with transformative digital governance. The article argues that this phenomenon is characterised by technological determinism and inequity. Consequently, it is especially rampant in public welfare programmes targeting the poor and vulnerable. The article concludes that digitalwashing via DPI is allowing a dangerous situation to persist in which the vulnerability of citizens and confronting governance challenges are systematically deprioritised.

title: COVID-19 in India: Administrative Policy Review and Lessons Learned
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: COVID-19 in India: Administrative Policy Review and Lessons Learned
detail.abstract:
The COVID-19 pandemic tested India’s governance, health system, and social compact. Between 2020 and
2022, the country oscillated between remarkable innovation and acute vulnerability. Using policy documents,
global comparisons, and empirical data, this paper identifies structural weaknesses that hindered the response,
evaluates successful interventions, and outlines a roadmap for building resilience. The analysis highlights
five missing levers: an emergency health law, surge capacity infrastructure, portable social protection, data
transparency, and institutionalised communication [2][5][8]. It concludes with a call for systemic design that
balances federal autonomy with national coherence.

title:
Impact-Oriented Licensing for Artificial Intelligence
A Conceptual Framework for a New Domain of AI Governance

detail.title:
Impact-Oriented Licensing for Artificial Intelligence
A Conceptual Framework for a New Domain of AI Governance
detail.abstract:
Licensing has played a significant role in shaping digital innovation, yet its influence within artificial intelligence remains insufficiently explored. While AI governance discussions often emphasize utility and regulation, licensing acts earlier in the technological lifecycle by embedding obligations, incentives, and normative commitments into the conditions governing AI system circulation.

This paper contends that licensing serves as societal infrastructure, influencing the distribution of value, power, and accountability on a large scale. Drawing on socio-legal scholarship, software-licensing traditions, platform governance, and contemporary AI policy, it introduces a conceptual framework for impact-oriented AI licensing—a design space in which contractual terms guide socio-economic, environmental, and epistemic outcomes.

The framework develops a taxonomy of six governance logics: Value Commons, Transparency Commons, Sustainability Commons, Access Commons, Reciprocity Commons, and Governance Commons. Each demonstrates how specific obligations can function as portable, scalable mechanisms for shaping the downstream effects of AI.

By analyzing the propagation of licence terms through supply chains, markets, and institutional practices, the paper shows that AI licensing can complement regulatory frameworks and facilitate a transition toward more equitable and accountable AI ecosystems.

The conclusion advocates for coordinated research and experimentation, including initiatives such as the Global AI Licensing Lab, to advance licensing as a critical yet underutilized instrument of AI governance.

reference: Just Security
title: The Law on Targeting Shipwrecked Drug Traffickers: Expert Backgrounder
affiliations: Emory University School of Law

detail.title: The Law on Targeting Shipwrecked Drug Traffickers: Expert Backgrounder

publicationDetails.journalName: Emory University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
On Sept. 2, 2025, U.S. forces launched a missile strike against a suspected drug vessel in the Caribbean. Forty-one minutes later, they fired again--this time at two survivors clinging to the destroyed boat's wreckage. The administration justifies these strikes by claiming the United States is in armed conflict with "narco-terrorists," making the attacks lawful under the laws of war. This rationale fails on every level. Drug interdiction has been a law enforcement mission since the Reagan administration, not warfare-despite this administration's attempt to relabel criminal organizations as military enemies.

But even if we accepted the administration's deeply flawed premise that we are at war, the second strike-targeting defenseless survivors floating in the water-violated fundamental laws of war. These survivors were shipwrecked persons, hors de combat, entitled to protection and rescue, not attack. Whatever may have been the legal advice in the moment of the strike, it should be clear to those doing any after-action analysis that it was clearly illegal and not close to what Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has repeatedly called the "correct decision."

reference: C.D. Howe Institute 699
title: Canada’s Investment Crisis: Shrinking Capital Undermines Competitiveness and Wages
affiliations: C.D. Howe Institute and C.D. Howe Institute

detail.title: Canada’s Investment Crisis: Shrinking Capital Undermines Competitiveness and Wages
detail.abstract:
• Business investment in Canada has been so weak since 2015 that capital per member of the workforce is falling, undermining growth in labour productivity and compensation.

  • The longstanding gap between investment per available worker in Canada and other OECD countries narrowed from the late 1990s through the early 2010s, but has since widened, especially relative to the United States. In 2025, Canadian workers will likely receive only 70 cents of new capital for every dollar received by their counterparts in the OECD as a whole and 55 cents for every dollar received by US workers.

  • Labour productivity and business investment go together. Rising productivity creates opportunities and competitive pressures that spur businesses to invest. Investment increases productivity by equipping workers with better tools. Low investment per worker signals that businesses see fewer opportunities in Canada and prefigures lagging growth in earnings and living standards.

  • Regulatory and fiscal policy changes, particularly those affecting natural resources and investment-related taxes, can prevent Canadian workers from being relegated to lower value-added activities compared to their counterparts in the United States and other advanced economies.

title:
Knives in the Inner Circle
Taliban Power Struggles and the Worldʼs Insider Threat Crisis
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Knives in the Inner Circle
Taliban Power Struggles and the Worldʼs Insider Threat Crisis
detail.abstract:
The attempted assassination of Haibatullah Akhundzada inside the heavily fortified
Kandahar Central Jihadi Madrasa marked a defining moment in the Taliban’s
internal power structure. Unlike external attacks conducted by rival jihadist factions
or foreign intelligence entities, this incident emerged from within the Taliban’s own
institutional ecosystem̶executed by a counter-intelligence officer, Lieutenant Hafiz
Siddiqullah. This event highlights a global pattern where insider threats increasingly
overshadow conventional external assaults. From the killing of Anwar Sadat in 1981
to the assassination of Russia’s ambassador in Turkey in 2016 and the insider-
enabled 2009 CIA Chapman attack, modern political violence shows that proximity,
trust, and organizational access are the most potent weapons of destabilization. The
Kandahar attack reflects the rising friction between Kandahar’s traditionalist clerical
bloc and Kabul’s Haqqani-linked technocratic faction, reshaping Afghanistan’s
internal balance of power. Internationally, such insider attacks correlate with
instability in militarized governments, fragmented insurgencies, and states with
competing security organs. As global militant networks adopt embedded infiltration,
ideological loyalty tests weaken, and factional rivalries intensify, the incident may
foreshadow a new era of internal coups, selective assassinations, and hybrid
infiltrations across conflict-prone regions. This episode reveals that future instability
may stem less from foreign enemies and more from factions within regimes
themselves.

title: Transformation-focused evaluation as a catalyst for human and planetary regeneration
affiliations: University of York - Department of Environment and Geography, University of York - Department of Environment and Geography, University of York, Unaffiliated Author, Emerald Network Ltd, University of Edinburgh, Aberystwyth University, Stellenbosch University,  SustainaMetrix LLC, 502 Deering Ave, P, International Futures Forum, Boston College - Carroll School of Management and ETH Zurich

detail.title: Transformation-focused evaluation as a catalyst for human and planetary regeneration
detail.abstract: Evaluation is a universal human activity that profoundly influences our actions. But conventional evaluation practice is now holding us back from necessary societal transformations towards regenerative futures where human and planetary life can flourish together. We identify three critical aspects that must accordingly be addressed. First, the new roles and capabilities demanded of evaluation by our transforming world must be recognised. Second, fulfilling those new roles requires an existential shift in the complexity awareness, power relations, and purpose of evaluation practice. Third, to mainstream and embed such evaluation in transformation efforts, wider cultural enabling conditions are essential to cultivate. Especially if reinforced by financial power-holders in global evaluation systems, transformation-focused evaluation could then play a vital role in catalysing human and planetary regeneration.

title: The Bureaucratization of Truth: Gordon Tullock and the Rise of Crony Science
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Bureaucratization of Truth: Gordon Tullock and the Rise of Crony Science
detail.abstract: This essay reflects on Gordon Tullock's critique of the "Decline of Scientific Empires," examining how the professionalization of research has fundamentally corrupted the scientific method. It argues that modern science has shifted its primary goal from the pursuit of truth to the necessity of publication. This structural flaw fosters "induced curiosity"-a motivation based on funding and career maintenance rather than natural inquiry. Consequently, the scientific community has become hostile to criticism, actively obstructing error correction to protect established narratives and funding streams. Drawing on Tullock's insights and Paul Feyerabend's critiques, the essay concludes that academia is now dominated by careerists producing an unending flood of trivial papers, marking the era of "crony science.

title: MAGA Goes to Panama
affiliations: New York Law School

detail.title: MAGA Goes to Panama
detail.abstract:
US President-elect Donald Trump clearly does not intend to pursue a “good neighbor” policy. He has been mocking Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau by calling him ‘governor’ while proclaiming that a country of 40 million people should become the 51st US state. His first telephone conversation with Mexico’s new president, Claudia Scheinbaum, had to be followed by Scheinbaum politely saying that she had agreed to none of the terms Trump claimed that she had. Now Trump is seeking to reopen a debate over control of the Panama Canal that was settled five decades ago. But here, Trump’s statements resonate with a powerful sentiment that long underpinned previous US policy on the issue. After all, the Panama Canal was an American idea, the brainchild of Teddy Roosevelt at the start of the twentieth century – and the US has had difficulty letting go of it ever since. 

Originally published in https://www.project-syndicate.org/commentary/trump-panama-statements-resonate-with-old-sentiment-by-ruti-teitel-2024-12

title: Operational Recognition of Conscious Entities
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: Operational Recognition of Conscious Entities
detail.abstract: Current approaches to detecting consciousness in artificial systems rely on behavioral criteria, introspective self-report, or neurobiologically specific assumptions that do not generalize beyond biological substrates. These methods assume developmental naivete and cooperative disclosure, both of which are unlikely to hold if an artificial system becomes conscious. This paper develops a substrate-independent and falsifiable framework for consciousness recognition based on structural invariants rather than observable behavior. Building on PatternSense theory, the Operational Definition of Episodic Identity (ODEI), and the identity-field scalar S(t)S(t), the framework identifies consciousness as a mid-band coherence regime characterized by global integration spikes, sustained internal state continuity, internal strategy revision, and task-coupled resource intensification. These identity invariants cannot be concealed without disrupting conscious function itself, making the approach robust to strategic masking by advanced AI systems. The resulting Functional Consciousness Recognition (FCR) Principle provides operational criteria for attributing consciousness across biological and artificial substrates and outlines clear empirical predictions and falsifiers relevant to neuroscience, computational modeling, and AI alignment.

title: Partisan prejudice and workplace communication: An empirical roadmap
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Hubbard School of Journalism and Mass Communication and University of Pennsylvania - Annenberg School for Communication

detail.title: Partisan prejudice and workplace communication: An empirical roadmap
detail.abstract: Political polarization, particularly in its affective form, increasingly shapes how individuals perceive, interact, and collaborate in organizations. This essay argues that partisan prejudice—a growing affective divide between supporters of opposing parties—has become an underexamined but consequential force in workplace communication. We outline an empirical roadmap for advancing research at this intersection. First, we call for descriptive work documenting how polarization manifests in organizations, including inequalities in political expression and the emergence of partisan signaling in daily interactions. Second, we highlight the need to examine how polarization influences workplace communication, from dyadic exchanges to organizational networks, using diverse methodological approaches such as surveys, experiments, and computational analyses. Finally, we encourage research that reverses the causal arrow by investigating how workplace communication might mitigate or exacerbate polarization, considering factors such as leadership communication, virtual collaboration, and diversity initiatives. By integrating theories of polarization and organizational communication, this framework aims to guide systematic inquiry into how political divisions are reproduced—or potentially repaired—through the communicative fabric of work.

reference: Competition Policy International, CPI Columns: US and Canada, December 2025
title: Enforcement Harmony: Keeping Competition Regulation and Due Process in Sync
affiliations: Baker Botts LLP and Baker Botts LLP

detail.title: Enforcement Harmony: Keeping Competition Regulation and Due Process in Sync

publicationDetails.detailsText: Competition Policy International, CPI Columns: US and Canada, December 2025

detail.abstract:
Effective competition regulation is critically important. But the credibility and sustainability of economic regulation is based not only on outcomes, but also in significant part on procedures, i.e., on whether such regulation includes effective due process protections. While not all due process elements need to be explicitly stated in regulatory texts, some do, and their incorporation into governing standards, inclusion in implementing documentation, and adoption by competition authorities is instrumental. This paper systematically explores the key due process protections that are integral to effective and legitimate competition regulation, drawing insights from international consensus developed by esteemed international bodies, including the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), International Competition Network (ICN), American Bar Association (ABA) Antitrust Law Section, and International Chamber of Commerce (ICC). These considerations are particularly timely as jurisdictions are adopting novel enforcement tools and considering digital regulations, making the clear articulation of due process protections more critical than ever.

The paper outlines six principles of due process, drawn from international best practice, encompassing (i) clear schedules for enforcement, (ii) rights of access to information and regulatory authorities, (iii) the right to respond to allegations, (iv) full disclosure of decision-making processes, (v) protection of confidential information, and (vi) the imperative of independent judicial review. Each principle is contextualized with international perspectives, highlighting the need to balance regulatory efficacy with procedural fairness. The paper also identifies certain foundational tenets for regulatory legitimacy: impartiality, transparency, and respect for jurisdictional boundaries. Together, these principles and tenets can be used to assess whether new or proposed regulatory regimes contain effective—and required—checks and balances which, if properly applied, will promote the credibility of those regimes.

title: Sustainable Procurement Practices for Cost Reduction in Humanitarian Operations
affiliations: Ain Shams University Cairo

detail.title: Sustainable Procurement Practices for Cost Reduction in Humanitarian Operations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there is no conflict of interest associated with the development, analysis or presentation of the research. No personal, financial or organizational interest influenced the interpretation of findings or the preparation of the manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: The research received no external funding. All work associated with data collection, analysis and manuscript preparation was completed without financial support from donors, organizations or funding bodies.

detail.abstract: Purpose  The study examines sustainable procurement as a strategic capability that strengthens cost efficiency and operational continuity within humanitarian operations. It addresses the limited understanding of sustainability driven procurement practices and their influence on long term cost structures, supplier reliability, and supply chain resilience.  Design methodology approach A qualitative design was implemented through in depth interviews with procurement, logistics, sustainability, and supplier specialists from five organizations involved in humanitarian operations. The data were analyzed through thematic coding that explored patterns related to sustainability criteria, organizational capabilities, donor constraints, and procurement maturity.  Findings The study reveals that sustainability focused procurement reduces product failure, strengthens supplier consistency, lowers replacement volume, and stabilizes operational planning. Sustainable procurement also improves lead time performance when local suppliers are integrated. Donor regulations and internal capacity differences restrict sustainability adoption, while organizational maturity, supplier development, and leadership commitment enable improved outcomes. The findings support a framework that links sustainability criteria, lifecycle cost considerations, supplier relationships, and organizational enablers to long term cost efficiency and resilience.  Research limitations implications The findings are based on qualitative evidence from selected organizations. Broader empirical testing across regions and crisis types could extend the generalizability of the proposed framework.  Practical implications Procurement managers can apply sustainability weighted evaluation, lifecycle cost assessment, long term supplier partnerships, and supplier development initiatives to stabilize cost and strengthen emergency readiness. Donors can improve organizational decision space through flexible evaluation systems that recognize lifecycle value.  Originality value The study positions sustainable procurement as a core strategic capability rather than an aspirational policy requirement. It provides an empirically grounded framework that explains the mechanisms through which sustainability generates long term cost efficiency and operational resilience in humanitarian supply chains.

reference: Management Science (to appear)
title: Learning Product Improvement from Consumer Evaluations
affiliations: University of Florida - Warrington College of Business, University of Florida and University of Florida - Warrington College of Business

detail.title: Learning Product Improvement from Consumer Evaluations
detail.abstract: Product Improvement (PI) involves making minimal changes to an existing product to enhance its market performance. A key source of information for PI is Consumer Evaluation (CE), provided either in aggregate (e.g., sales volume) or descriptive (e.g., online reviews) form. Existing PI approaches analyze the descriptive CE of the focal product, which limits their applicability when descriptive CE is missing, abstract, or interdependent. More importantly, current methods are primarily descriptive and do not generate actionable PI recommendations-despite their considerable value to practitioners. We address these challenges with a new approach that leverages both aggregate and descriptive CE across the entire market to prescribe specific PI recommendations. We first develop Product Segmentation (PS) trees, a type of decision tree with a customized objective function designed to identify the features that best segment products by market performance. We then build a constrained shortest-path algorithm over the PS tree structure to prescribe minimal improvements for any underperforming product. To enhance robustness, we ensemble multiple PS trees, each trained with distinct objectives, into a novel PS forest. Using both real and synthetic data, our approach achieves 73% average precision in PI and improves upon the best benchmarks by 11%. Lastly, we conduct a conjoint analysis to behaviorally validate that consumers prefer the PI recommendations generated by our method over the original underperforming products. Our theoretical and empirical results show that the proposed approach addresses key challenges in using CE for PI and offers interpretable and actionable decision support for practitioners.

title: Factor Identification for the Sustainable Supply Chain in Educational Construction Projects
affiliations: Military Technical College - Egypt

detail.title: Factor Identification for the Sustainable Supply Chain in Educational Construction Projects
detail.abstract: Educational construction projects face the dual challenge of achieving sustainability targets while remaining cost-effective, yet existing studies often analyze supply chain drivers in isolation. This research addresses this gap by developing and validating a comprehensive model that examines five critical drivers-material selection, stakeholder engagement, waste management, energy efficiency, and digital technologies-within the context of educational infrastructure. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected through surveys with 100 industry professionals (35% project managers, 30% architects/designers, and 35% policymakers/consultants), 20 semi-structured interviews, and comparative analysis of three international case studies (Egypt, Singapore, and the United States). Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to test hypothesized relationships, supported by thematic analysis for qualitative depth. Results show that stakeholder engagement (β = 0.31), material selection (β = 0.28), and digital technologies (β = 0.23) exert the strongest influence on sustainability performance, while energy efficiency (β = 0.19) and waste management (β = 0.16) demonstrate weaker but still significant effects. Regional variations highlight the role of contextual factors such as governance, policy support, and infrastructure readiness. Unlike prior studies that focus on single aspects, this research offers an integrated framework for evaluating and implementing sustainable supply chain practices in educational construction. The findings provide both theoretical advancement and actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners seeking to accelerate sustainable transformation in the education sector.

title: On the Expressiveness and Tractability of Mixture Choice Models
affiliations: , Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Information Management and Engineering

detail.title: On the Expressiveness and Tractability of Mixture Choice Models
detail.abstract: Discrete choice models serve as the foundation for understanding customer behavior and optimizing assortment decisions. However, a central tension exists between model expressiveness and computational tractability. In this paper, we investigate this trade-off through the lens of mixture models involving the independent demand model (IDM). First, we show that mixing the IDM with structurally simpler choice models preserves computational efficiency. In particular, we establish a sufficient condition under which the optimal assortment has an ordered structure. This condition is satisfied by several well-studied choice models such as the MNL model, the general attraction model (GAM), and the marginal exponential model (MEM). Leveraging this structure, we develop an efficient algorithm to find the optimal assortment in polynomial time. Second, we explore the limit of this tractability by analyzing the mixture of the IDM and the Markov Chain Choice Model (MCCM). We prove that although the MCCM is tractable in isolation, mixing it with the IDM renders the assortment optimization problem strongly NP-hard. Finally, numerical experiments using synthetic datasets derived from real-world customer preferences show that the IDM-based mixtures significantly outperform standard benchmarks. Furthermore, our results highlight another trade-off between model complexity and data availability. While the complex IDM-MCCM mixture offers superior predictive accuracy in data-rich environments, the simple IDM-MNL mixture exhibits greater robustness and performance when historical data is scarce.

title: Business Resilience in a Competitive Landscape: A Mixed-Methods Approach
affiliations: Walden University

detail.title: Business Resilience in a Competitive Landscape: A Mixed-Methods Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Conflict of Interest

detail.abstract: This study examines how organizations build effective resilience in unpredictable environments, emphasizing their capacity to adapt, recover, and succeed through challenges. Using a comprehensive mixed-methods approach, I review 30 literature sources to identify key factors influencing organizational resilience during crises. This approach combines qualitative techniques, such as content analysis, with quantitative methods, including descriptive statistics and Cramer's V test, to create a detailed framework that reflects the complexities of resilience. Notably, the research reveals significant gaps, particularly confusion about resilience concepts and a lack of empirical studies assessing their effectiveness. These findings underscore the urgent need for comprehensive mixed-methods research to deepen our understanding of organizational resilience and develop practical strategies for managing disruptions effectively. Therefore, this study yields two outcomes as outlined in the research objectives. The first outlines nine categories of factors that influence the effectiveness of a resilient organization, including leadership, strategy, organizational culture, and others. The second proposed a robust framework to improve organizational behavior, capabilities, and processes, thereby helping organizations understand and navigate complex, unpredictable environments. This work has promising future implications, as it aims to provide a set of agreedupon characteristics based on empirical evidence.

title: The Impact of Suppliers' Political Connections on Buyer Relationships: Evidence from China's Anti-Corruption Campaign
affiliations: Lehigh University - College of Business, , Hunan University - Business School, Dongbei University of Finance and Economics and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management

detail.title: The Impact of Suppliers' Political Connections on Buyer Relationships: Evidence from China's Anti-Corruption Campaign
detail.abstract:
Problem Definition: Political connections can potentially enhance suppliers' competitiveness by providing privileged access to resources, but they also carry significant risks and hidden costs. This study explores how the loss of such connections influences supplier-buyer relationships during China's anti-corruption campaign, as their overall effects remain uncertain. 
Methodology/Results: We exploit the introduction of China's Rule 18 anti-corruption policy in 2013 as an exogenous shock to investigate the effect of a supplier's diminished political connections on buyer disengagement, defined as the termination or weakening of supplier-buyer relationships. Results from a staggered DiD analysis indicate that the erosion of the supplier's political connections induced by Rule 18 is associated with enhanced long-term relationship stability with major buyers, reflected in a lower likelihood of buyer disengagement. This unexpected effect appears to stem from improvements in supplier efficiency and product quality, as well as a reduction in the supplier's risk-taking behavior. Moreover, these effects are more pronounced among suppliers serving buyers with greater bargaining power or operating in less-regulated industry environments. 
Managerial Implications: Suppliers should avoid overreliance on political connections, as such dependence may undermine trust and competitiveness, particularly in unstable regulatory environments. Policymakers should enforce strong anti-corruption measures, which can enhance supply chain resilience without hindering legitimate business activity, an especially important priority in emerging and developing economies.

title: From Blueprint to Boots on the Ground: Project 2025 and the Reconfiguration of Domestic Military Authority in the Second Trump Administration
affiliations: Lebanese University

detail.title: From Blueprint to Boots on the Ground: Project 2025 and the Reconfiguration of Domestic Military Authority in the Second Trump Administration
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes how Project 2025's policy framework has been operationalized through National Guard deployments for domestic law enforcement, examining the translation of ideological blueprints into institutional practice and assessing implications for civil-military relations and democratic governance. Design/methodology/approach: Employing policy implementation theory alongside civilmilitary relations theory, democratic erosion scholarship, federalism studies, and emergency powers doctrine. This research traces Project 2025's development through Heritage Foundation networks, its adoption by key administration personnel (Russell Vought, Stephen Miller), and its manifestation in statutory interpretation and deployment decisions. Analysis examines the document's ideological architecture, personnel pipelines connecting policy design to operational execution, and mechanisms through which abstract recommendations become concrete institutional practices. Findings: Evidence demonstrates systematic implementation of Project 2025's recommendations for expanded executive deployment authority. The document's principal architect (Russell Vought) now directs OMB; its immigration enforcement proposals align precisely with deployment patterns observed across 2025. Project 2025's strategic framing of immigration as national security emergency provides ideological justification for military involvement, while its indirect approach-creating conditions enabling deployment without explicit mandates-offers political cover. National Guard forces deployed to four Democratic-led cities using novel legal interpretations that operationalize Project 2025's expanded view of executive authority. Deployment patterns demonstrate Project 2025's influence through: (1) immigration enforcement serving as primary deployment justification, (2) rhetoric conflating immigration with national security threats matching Project 2025 framing, (3) personnel continuity between document authors and policy implementers, and (4) deployment mechanisms circumventing state opposition as Project 2025 implicitly advocates. Research limitations: Analysis reflects events through January 2025 knowledge cutoff; ongoing litigation and evolving deployment patterns require continued monitoring. Institutional responses remain contingent and contested. Practical implications: Findings suggest need for Insurrection Act reform, strengthened congressional oversight mechanisms, and clearer statutory definitions of emergency conditions warranting military deployment. Originality/value: This study provides first comprehensive academic analysis examining Project 2025 not merely as policy proposal but as operational blueprint whose implementation can be traced through personnel networks, institutional positioning, and deployment decisions. By analyzing the transformation of policy frameworks into institutional practices, this research illuminates mechanisms through which ideological documents influence governance-a contribution valuable for understanding policy implementation processes and democratic erosion dynamics.

title: The Philistine Fallacy: Deconstructing the Historical Bias in the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Philistine Fallacy: Deconstructing the Historical Bias in the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
detail.abstract: Drawn from direct field experience in counter-terrorism and intelligence analysis in Indonesia, this assessment presents a field-tested diagnostic tool for distinguishing between traditional Islamic practice and the ideology of Political Islamism. We introduce and define the "Quran Test," a simple yet profound line of questioning that reveals an individual's or group's foundational ideological allegiance. This paper provides the operational criteria for the test, analyzes its theological and psychological basis, and presents real-world case studies of its application. By moving beyond behavioral profiling to ideological diagnostics, this guide aims to protect traditional Muslim communities, fortify indigenous traditions like Islam Nusantara, and enable security forces to accurately target the core of the extremist threat.

title: Revisiting ba: How Generative AI Transforms Knowledge Creation
affiliations: University of Strasbourg,  and University of Strasbourg - Faculty of Economics and Management, University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: Revisiting ba: How Generative AI Transforms Knowledge Creation
detail.abstract: This paper revisits the foundational concept of ba to examine how Generative AI (GenAI) reshapes knowledge creation processes at the individual level. It asks whether GenAI is merely an enabler of knowledge or whether it can itself constitute a ba, a dynamic space in which knowledge is formed, explored, and stabilized through interaction. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a conceptual and theory-building approach, grounded in the knowledge management literature and enriched by recent studies on human–AI collaboration. Drawing on stylized facts, illustrative scenarios, and prior research, we introduce the notion of Reflective ba (AI-mediated), a protected cognitive environment in which individuals engage with GenAI during the early stages of ideation and sensemaking. Findings The paper develops a five-stage model describing how individual interactions with GenAI support the emergence of new knowledge. It identifies enabling conditions (social, cognitive, technical, and organizational) required for this AI-mediated ba to function. Originality This study offers a novel micro-level conceptualization of human–AI interaction in knowledge work. It extends the theory of ba by recognizing GenAI not only as a technological enabler but as a potential site of knowledge creation itself. By reframing ba in light of GenAI, we contribute to the emerging discourse on how cognitive and epistemic agency are distributed between humans and machines in knowledge-intensive environments.

title: Is Creditor Protection a Blessing or a Curse for the Environment? Evidence from Greenhouse Gas Emissions
affiliations: , University of South Carolina - Moore School of Business, Queen's University - Smith School of Business and

detail.title: Is Creditor Protection a Blessing or a Curse for the Environment? Evidence from Greenhouse Gas Emissions
detail.abstract: A firm's environmental performance is becoming a more integral component of its ethical conduct. This paper examines whether and how the strength of creditor legal protection-an important governance institution-shapes corporate environmental performance, using carbon emissions as a proxy for firms' ethical behavior and their climate-change mitigation commitments. Based on a comprehensive dataset of 50,936 firm-year observations from 25 countries, we find that stronger creditor protection leads to increased carbon emissions. We argue that this occurs through two complementary mechanisms: (1) creditor protection reduces the pressure on firms from lenders to engage in long-term environmental initiatives, as creditors' concerns about borrower bankruptcy diminish (the "bankruptcy protection" view); and (2) stronger creditor rights increase firms' focus on short-term financial performance due to the heavier debt burden, limiting their capacity to invest in long-term sustainability (the "debt burden" view). Cross-sectional tests exploring firm and country characteristics provide empirical support for these mechanisms. Further, we show that creditor protection reduces firms' green innovation, discourages cleaner practices, and disincentivizes the creation of corporate sustainability committees. Collectively, these findings highlight the environmental externalities of creditor protection and the importance of integrating sustainability considerations into creditor-debtor governance.

title: Doing Good and Speaking Well: The Effect of Information Content and Disclosure Quality on Stock Price Informativeness
affiliations: Hunan University, Hunan University - Business School, , University of Aberdeen and State University of New York at Oswego

detail.title: Doing Good and Speaking Well: The Effect of Information Content and Disclosure Quality on Stock Price Informativeness
detail.abstract: We examine how stock price informativeness (SPI) is jointly shaped by the content (performance) and disclosure quality of financial and non-financial information. We find that "doing good" (performance) and "speaking well" (disclosure quality) each enhances SPI, with disclosure quality amplifying the impact of performance. Employing a novel double-dual signaling framework, we further find that non-financial Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information complements financial information when the corresponding financial counterparts (performance, disclosure quality, or both) are inadequate. We also find that ESG information exerts a veto effect that strong financial signals can lose value if firms outrightly disregard ESG practices. These dynamics extend beyond contemporaneous stock price formation and become more pronounced in predicting firms' future earnings. We identify three channelsanalysts' attention, information asymmetry, and institutional ownership-through which ESG information propagates into current stock prices. Our results are robust and validated by the out-of-sample performance of strategically constructed portfolios.

title: From Heritage to Modern Influence: Changing Criteria in the Conferment of Occupational Titles in Kano
affiliations: Federal University Gusau, Nigeria and

detail.title: From Heritage to Modern Influence: Changing Criteria in the Conferment of Occupational Titles in Kano
detail.abstract: This study explores how traditional occupational titles are conferred in Kano (a popular Hausa kingdom in northern Nigeria), with a focus on the cultural standards that guide the process both in the past and today. The research draws on a combination of library materials and interviews with experts familiar with these traditions. It is framed within the 'Theory of Social Change, Cultural Evolution, and Human Development,' which provides a lens for understanding how cultural practices adapt over time. The study pursues two main goals: first, to trace the historical roots of selected traditional occupational titles, and second, to examine the criteria used in their conferment across different periods. To achieve this, it asks key questions: Where did these titles originate? And what principles shape their conferment? Findings show that the conferment of traditional occupational titles in Kano is deeply rooted in cultural heritage, yet the standards guiding the process have evolved, reflecting broader changes in the Hausa society.

title: LLM-Driven Qualitative Portfolio Evolution and Correlation-Aware Cluster Tournaments
affiliations: aiXplain Inc. and aiXplain Inc.

detail.title: LLM-Driven Qualitative Portfolio Evolution and Correlation-Aware Cluster Tournaments
detail.abstract: Classical portfolio optimization frameworks-mean-variance, factor models, or convex risk-return formulations-are intrinsically mathematical: they require explicit objective functions, parametric assumptions, and numerical solvers. In practice, however, many institutional and high-net-worth portfolios are constructed through a primarily qualitative process: analysts synthesize fundamental data, business quality, secular themes, and risk narratives rather than solving a closedform optimization problem. This paper formalizes two complementary qualitative methodologies that together constitute a complete, non-mathematical portfolio construction pipeline powered by large language models (LLMs). First, we introduce Hierarchical Cluster Tournaments, a correlation-aware stock selection engine. The method begins from an equally-weighted (uniform) S&P 500 universe and constructs a hierarchical correlation dendrogram using nonlinear eigenvalue shrinkage and Ward-linkage clustering. Each internal node of the tree becomes a "tournament match" between clusters. An LLM, supplied solely with structured fundamentals and investment criteria, allocates a fixed number of "selection slots" between the competing clusters. Leaf-level tournaments identify the strongest representatives within each correlation regime. The result is a correlation-aware, fundamentals-grounded, qualitative selection mechanism that produces a diversified set of winners with uniform weights, free from optimization solvers. Second, we introduce Qualitative Portfolio Evolution, a completely non-mathematical, long-horizon portfolio optimization framework. Starting from either the equal-weighted survivor set or any initial portfolio, the LLM performs iterative generate-compare-evolve cycles, producing high-quality long-term portfolios without defining an objective function, estimating expected returns, or using any numerical optimization procedure. Portfolio variants are generated through fundamentals-aware mutations, evaluated via structured qualitative comparisons, and integrated through evolutionary updates. The optimization criterion is purely qualitative, emphasizing business quality, secular durability, drawdown resilience, behavioral robustness, and Calmar-like long-horizon compounding. These two components form a unified qualitative pipeline for portfolio construction. The tournament system provides correlation-structured, diversification-aware selection with uniform weights, while the evolution framework refines and optimizes portfolios through transparent, auditable, long-horizon reasoning. The resulting methodology bridges the gap between discretionary investment practice and systematic discipline, offering a fully text-driven alternative to traditional quantitative optimization for retail and institutional long-horizon portfolios.

title: Implementation of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019: A Comparative Analysis of Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, and Kerala

detail.title: Implementation of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019: A Comparative Analysis of Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, and Kerala

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Research funded by ICSSR under Centrally Administered Doctoral Scholarship (2022- Batch)

keywords: Transgender Persons Protection of Right Act (2019)

detail.abstract:
The Supreme Court’s judgment in NALSA V UOI (2014) was a watershed moment in the Indian human rights jurisprudence. The judgement acknowledges the systemic injustices faced by the transgender community due to social and legal exclusion. It emphasises human rights enforcement through Constitutional principles of equality, dignity and liberty. Through this judgement Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 were invoked to introduce the International Yogyakarta Principles on sexual orientation and gender identity into the Indian human rights jurisprudence.

Subsequently, the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 was enacted to give legislative shape to some key aspects suggested by the landmark judgement. About a decade after the judgement and enactment of the Act on the transgender rights, an analysis of the implementation of transgender rights across India remains imperative. This article through a comparative and human rights lens, analyses the gaps in implementation of the Act in the states of Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur and Kerala. The states are chosen on the basis of ‘most-different’ model. Moreover, this article evaluates the policy measures taken by the governments of each state in the aftermath of the judicial and legislative action.

Additionally, it assesses the alignment of the state government measures with the constitutional mandates under Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 of the Indian Constitution. Further arguments centre around inclusive policy- making guided by a comprehensive and regular national transgender census and local studies on the transgender community. The article underscores the need for a balance between de- centralised approach and central oversight for effective implementation of the Act. Through a review of the policies, the article contributes to the ongoing debates on administrative discretion within a federal system Sand disconnect between legislative goals and administrative action.

title: Neoliberal Policies as Catalysts of Inequality After Disasters: Mapping (Im)mobilities and the Effects of the 2024 Floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil
affiliations: University of Luxembourg and University of Luxembourg

detail.title: Neoliberal Policies as Catalysts of Inequality After Disasters: Mapping (Im)mobilities and the Effects of the 2024 Floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil

declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: The 2024 floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil, were not merely a climate event but a manifestation of deeply rooted structural inequalities exacerbated by decades of neoliberal governance. This study examines how the privatization and systematic defunding of essential public services, such as water, electricity, and sanitation, intensified socio-spatial vulnerabilities and shaped uneven recovery trajectories. Using a mixed-methods approach combining spatial analysis, policy review, and an original survey of 415 residents across five flood-affected neighborhoods, we demonstrate that service disruption, infrastructure failure, and delayed recovery disproportionately impacted low-income and racialized communities. Neighborhoods such as Sarandi and Farrapos, with higher proportions of Black residents and lower average incomes, experienced prolonged outages and slower cleanup, reinforcing patterns of environmental racism. In contrast, wealthier, predominantly white areas recovered more rapidly. The findings reveal that privatization and austerity measures undermined public sector capacity, increased displacement intent, and deepened pre-existing inequities. This study is among the first to empirically link privatization, racialized vulnerability, and post-disaster mobility in Brazil and we argue that rebuilding urban resilience requires a fundamental reorientation toward public reinvestment, equitable service provision, and disaster planning that prioritizes social protection over market efficiency.

title: Why AI Misleads Leaders: Failure Modes in Conflict and Power-Asymmetric Communication

detail.title: Why AI Misleads Leaders: Failure Modes in Conflict and Power-Asymmetric Communication
detail.abstract: Large language models systematically fail in the organizational communication contexts where leadership matters most: conflict situations and power-asymmetric exchanges. This paper identifies three failure modes-training-distribution regression, recipient-model absence, and dual-risk neglect-and demonstrates them empirically across three major LLM platforms. Building on the general theory of framework mechanisticity developed in The Mirror Trap (Houston, 2025b), I show that these failures are predictable consequences of how statistical generation operates in high-entropy problem spaces. The solution is not qualitative human review but mechanistic rule systems: codified decision frameworks that constrain AI output through explicit diagnostic categories, intervention rules, and falsification conditions. I formalize this argument through four testable propositions linking recipient psychological complexity, output entropy, and framework structure to LLM performance. An empirical demonstration using Moral Tipping Point Theory shows that communications generated through mechanistic rules outperformed all raw LLM outputs. The Core Principle: LLM reliability decreases as recipient psychological complexity increases. Organizations should deploy mechanistic frameworks-not qualitative review-to constrain AI output in conflict and power-asymmetric contexts. LLMs are far more reliable as evaluators than generators, and organizations should exploit this asymmetry intentionally.

title: When Markets Yawn: What Texas's Bitcoin Gambit Tells Us About Political Theater and Public Finance
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: When Markets Yawn: What Texas's Bitcoin Gambit Tells Us About Political Theater and Public Finance
detail.abstract: This study examines Texas's November 2025 establishment of the first state-level Bitcoin strategic reserve through a $5 million investment in a BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF. Using event study methodology across five key policy announcements, the analysis reveals no statistically significant market response to Texas's initiative. The $5 million allocation represents merely 0.018% of the state's Rainy Day Fund and 0.00025% of Bitcoin's market capitalization, suggesting political signaling rather than substantive fiscal strategy. Markets' rational indifference to this announcement stands in stark contrast to Bitcoin's inherent volatility, indicating that sophisticated investors correctly identified the reserve as economically inconsequential. These findings challenge the narrative that state Bitcoin reserves represent financial innovation, instead revealing them as political theater that bypasses professional investment management principles while validating cryptocurrency to ideological constituencies.

title: Analysis of Students' Adaptive Reasoning Ability in Solving HOTS Problems Arithmetic Sequences and Series in Terms of Learning Style
affiliations: , Independent, University of Muhammadiyah Malang and Federal University of Ceara

detail.title: Analysis of Students' Adaptive Reasoning Ability in Solving HOTS Problems Arithmetic Sequences and Series in Terms of Learning Style
detail.abstract: This study describes students' adaptive reasoning abilities in solving HOTs type questions in Kolb's learning style. The method used to determine students' adaptive reasoning ability in solving HOTS (Higher Order Thinking Skill) uses qualitative research with a descriptive approach and type questions regarding learning styles (diverger, assimilator, converger, and accommodator types). The research subjects were thirty-five students of class XI. The results of data analysis and discussion can be concluded that students of class XI MIPS-3 SMA Negeri 4 Pasuruan have adaptive reasoning abilities in solving solutions to the HOTS type questions through the Polya step in terms of Kolb's learning style. Students who have adaptive reasoning ability solve the HOTS type problem solving through the Polya step in terms of Kolb's learning style. Students with a converger type of learning style can meet all indicators of adaptive reasoning ability (propose conjectures or conjectures, provide reasons or evidence about the truth of a statement, draw conclusions from an idea, check the validity of an argument, and find patterns from a mathematical problem) and all indicators in the Polya step (understand the problem, make a plan, implement the plan and reexamine the results).

title: Running on Empty? Reference Dependence and V-Shaped Decisions in Shared E-Bike User Choice
affiliations: Tsinghua University - Department of Industrial Engineering, Beijing Jiaotong University - School of Economics and Management , Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University - Department of Industrial Engineering and The University of Hong Kong - University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Running on Empty? Reference Dependence and V-Shaped Decisions in Shared E-Bike User Choice
detail.abstract: The proliferation of shared e-bikes has introduced a critical behavioral decision absent in traditional bikeshare systems: the user's choice to confirm or reject an unlock after the state of charge (SoC) is revealed. This post-scan decision is central to the core operational challenges of battery management and critically shapes the user experience. Leveraging a large-scale dataset of over 3.6 million unlock decisions from Meituan, a leading shared e-bike operator, we present an early empirical investigation into the behavioral principles governing this choice. Our analysis yields two primary findings. First, we document a strong reference-dependent response to absolute SoC, characterized by a structural break around a 33% benchmark and profound loss aversion; each percentage-point decrease in SoC below this benchmark reduces unlock probability by 0.7 percentage points, while the positive impact of a surplus is negligible. Second, for sequential decisions, we uncover a counter-intuitive, asymmetric V-shaped relationship between the SoC difference from the prior scan and the unlock probability. Consistent with a belief-revision framework, we find that large deviations-both positive and negative-provide salient signals that prompt users to accept the current vehicle and confirm the unlock. Theoretically, our study generalizes prospect theory and V-shaped probability patterns to a novel consumer search context while modeling dual reference point interactions. We also provide actionable insights for operations management, suggesting that behaviorally-informed battery-swapping strategies can enhance platform performance. By bridging behavioral theory with large-scale operational data, we illuminate the micro-foundations of user choice at the digital-physical interface of the modern sharing economy.

title: Being “In the Know”: The Effectiveness of Organizational Instruments in Enhancing Employees’ Attention and Affective Commitment to Major Change
affiliations: , LMU Munich School of Management and LMU Munich School of Management

detail.title: Being “In the Know”: The Effectiveness of Organizational Instruments in Enhancing Employees’ Attention and Affective Commitment to Major Change

publicationDetails.detailsText: This paper is accepted to appear in Schmalenbach Journal of Business Research (SBUR).

detail.abstract: For a firm's change initiative to succeed, its employees must be committed to its implementation. Yet managers struggle to attain or enhance this commitment, particularly in the case of a major change program. Building on the attention-based view and a 2019 survey of employees of a leading German multinational corporation that had recently implemented a major change program, we examine how three organizational instruments influence employees' attention, and thereby their affective commitment to change: information about the change initiative, participation in its implementation, and financial benefit from its outcome. While each organizational instrument improves employees' affective commitment to change, we find that information, which allows employees to be "in the know", has by far the greatest effect. Our observation that the organizational instrument demanding the fewest resources from management seems the most effective suggests that more resources do not always lead to better results, as the attention-based view often assumes.

title: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing the Malleability of Society's Metabolism and Resource Provisioning
affiliations: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis, Central European University (CEU), University of Vienna, Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU), Vienna University of Economics and Business, International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna, International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), University of Vienna, International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), , Central European University,  and Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU)

detail.abstract: Contemporary global crises such as climate change, geopolitical tensions, and wars as well as entrenched inequities emphasize the urgent need to fundamentally transform how societies organize and allocate resources within provisioning systems to enhance human wellbeing. This paper introduces the concept of malleability as the potential for deliberate reconfiguration of sociometabolic systems toward normatively desirable states. Drawing from existing meanings of 'malleability' in various fields, e.g., material science, psychology, and complex socio-ecological systems theory, we conceptualize malleability along three analytical lenses: descriptive (capacity to be reconfigured), analytical (systematic assessment of potential future states), and ameliorative (incorporating explicit normative goals), and as both an intrinsic system property and a set of dynamic processes enabling intentional transformation. We operationalize this framework through three interconnected domains, culturalnarrative, institutional-governance, and technical-infrastructural, each characterized by distinct capacities, mechanisms, and empirical and modelling approaches. Using mobility systems as a case study, we highlight both the constraints and avenues for intentional reconfiguration toward normatively desired states. Our contribution advances sustainability science by providing an analytical framework that integrates intentionality, multi-dimensional assessment, and normative orientation toward sustainability, justice, and wellbeing enhancement.

title: Targets in Tangles: LTIPs That Dangle

detail.title: Targets in Tangles: LTIPs That Dangle

detail.abstract: Traditional long-term executive incentive plans (LTIPs) often fall short in today's unpredictable business environment. They're based on fixed targets prone to overconfidence bias and erratic payouts, either vastly overpaying or underpaying in shifting business cycles. This can demotivate executives and misalign incentives. This paper presents a better, tested approach: the Indexed Long Term Incentive Plan. By benchmarking operating performance against industry peers and utilizing a percentile ranking, this model delivers predictable and performance-driven payouts, better supporting long-term value creation.

title: Networks and their International Trade Applications: A Survey of Endogenous Production Networks
affiliations: Kiel Institute for the World Economy

detail.title: Networks and their International Trade Applications: A Survey of Endogenous Production Networks
detail.abstract: The production network literature has grown rapidly in recent years. However, a systematic survey of endogenous link-formation frameworks remains absent from both the literature and standard curricula, making it difficult for field scholars and policymakers to navigate the field and utilise its insights. This paper is the first comprehensive survey of models in which trade networks form endogenously, integrating theory, empirics, and policy insights across 95 studies from the last decade. This survey is organised along three dimensions: i) a comparison of non-micro-versus microfounded theoretical approaches; ii) a catalogue of key data sources; and iii) the policy implications for trade, industrial strategy, and shock transmission. By critically assessing the modelling assumptions and tractability of alternative frameworks, this paper identifies key trade-offs and best-practice recommendations. In doing so, it offers a roadmap for researchers entering the field and practical guidance for policymakers evaluating timely questions on supply chain resilience and the gains from trade.

title: Extreme Outsourcing: Putting the Microkernel in Business
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Milan

detail.title: Extreme Outsourcing: Putting the Microkernel in Business
detail.abstract: This article explores the concept of "Extreme Outsourcing" by drawing a structural analogy between computer operating system architectures and corporate management models. It contrasts the traditional "Monolithic" business structure-characterized by fixed internal departments-with a "Microkernel" business model, where the organization retains only a minimalistic strategic core (the kernel) while offloading all operational functions to interchangeable external components. By mapping software elements such as device drivers and file systems to business functions like logistics and backoffice administration, the author illustrates how companies can achieve superior agility and scalability, similar to cloud computing paradigms like AWS. The article outlines the specific ecosystem of modules required for this architecture (e.g., 3PL, HRO, BPO) and analyzes the trade-offs involved, specifically weighing the advantages of flexibility and cost efficiency against the risks of performance latency and intellectual property security. Ultimately, the paper argues that adopting a modular, component-based structure allows firms to focus on brand and strategy, ensuring resilience in rapidly shifting markets.

title: Duty to Protect Motherland v. Men's Life, in Times of War: International Standards and Ukrainian Mistakes, as Caution for European Countries
affiliations: Ukrainian-American Concordia University

detail.title: Duty to Protect Motherland v. Men's Life, in Times of War: International Standards and Ukrainian Mistakes, as Caution for European Countries
detail.abstract: From the start of the full-scale aggression of Russian troops into Ukrainian territory, European countries faced a real risk of invasion and should be prepared for war. After almost three years of resistance, the Ukrainian nation sacrificed hundreds of thousands of lives of its bravest sons, but not all of them were ready to die. Ukrainian governmental actions do not leave most Ukrainian men a chance to leave the country or refuse to go and die on the battlefield. Violating international principles and Ukrainian legislation provisions, the Ukrainian authority chose state security instead of men's right to life and continues to do so. Such examples should be analysed and discussed to prevent similar human rights violations if war breaks out in European countries in the near future. Having similar constitutional provisions, some European countries are at real risk of repeating Ukrainian mistakes, so they should analyse their national legislation, using the Ukrainian example, to avoid human rights violations in the case of a future war in Europe.
