detail.abstract: This module provides an in-depth exploration of money, banking, and financial systems, with strong emphasis on Rwanda’s rapidly transforming financial sector. Students examine traditional and modern concepts of money, the structure and regulation of financial institutions, and national monetary policy operations as implemented by the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR). The module integrates global theoretical frameworks with Rwandan policy realities such as financial inclusion initiatives, digital payment ecosystems, exchange rate policy, and financial sector reforms under Vision 2050.

title: Reconstructing Algorithmic Trading in the Age of Generative AI: Implications for Market Structure, Regulation, and Epistemology
affiliations: Externado de Colombia University

detail.title: Reconstructing Algorithmic Trading in the Age of Generative AI: Implications for Market Structure, Regulation, and Epistemology
detail.abstract:
Accepted for publication at Revista Emercatoria December 2025

The purpose of this article is to analyse how generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI)– defined here as systems capable of producing novel outputs, such as text, code, or data, through machine learning– is transforming algorithmic trading. Gen AI enhances computational efficiency but also reconfigures the epistemological (theories of knowledge), institutional (market structures and actors), and regulatory (rules and oversight) foundations of financial markets. We contend that Gen AI ushers in a shift from price as a representation of economic fundamentals to price as a recursive output of machine-to-machine simulation. Drawing on lessons from financial machine learning, critical legal theory, political economy, and the sociology of finance, we study how generative models– such as transformer-based architectures (deep learning models initially developed for natural language processing) and synthetic data engines (tools generating artificial datasets)– reshape the logic of price discovery, liquidity provision, and risk assessment. Our analysis shows that Gen – AI intensifies market abstraction, undermines traditional regulatory assumptions, and consolidates informational power among a narrow elite of technologically sophisticated actors. It sheds light on epistemic opacity, feedback loops, and algorithmic reflexivity. These features compromise both market intelligibility and regulatory legitimacy. We also pay particular attention to how these dynamics exacerbate global inequalities. This happens through infrastructure asymmetries and imports regulatory templates that marginalize the global south.We conclude by urging the implementation of new regulations that prioritize clarity, accountability, and digital control. We suggest reforms such as public model registries, participatory audits, and open algorithmic infrastructure to restore democratic oversight in markets increasingly run by code. Our goal is to reposition algorithmic trading as a central arena for debates about value, governance, and economic reality in synthetic finance.

title: Does the new quality productivity enhance the trade and investment promotion effect of the construction of   China pilot free trade zone?
affiliations: Guangxi University, Guangxi University,  and

detail.title: Does the new quality productivity enhance the trade and investment promotion effect of the construction of   China pilot free trade zone?
detail.abstract: Constructing the foreign trade and investment index of the pilot free trade zone (PFTZ) to measure the foreign trade and investment of the cities in the zone, it is found that the foreign trade and investment of the cities in the zone of China Pilot Free Trade Zone show a steady upward trend, with the highest level in the eastern coastal cities, followed by the inland cities, and lastly the cities along the borders. Based on the theoretical analysis and research hypothesis of the relationship between the construction of the pilot free trade zone and the city's foreign trade and investment, as well as the role of the new quality productivity in it, the generalized synthetic control method is used to evaluate and find that the construction of the pilot free trade zone has a significant promoting effect on the expansion of the foreign trade and investment activities of the cities in the area. Further empirical analysis with the adjustment effect model shows that the development of new quality productivity, including the new quality labor force, new quality labor object and new quality production means, significantly improves the promotion effect, and the new quality labor force has the largest effect. The study also found that there is regional variability in the promotion effect of new quality productivity, and the promotion effect of new quality productivity is more significant in the eastern coastal region. In addition, the promotion effect of the three components of new quality productivity is also regionally heterogeneous. Finally, based on the above analysis, the study proposes to accelerate the construction of the pilot free trade zone to promote the further development of foreign trade and investment in the cities in the zone; to promote the development of new quality productivity; and to strengthen regional development and coordination based on the differentiated characteristics of different regions.

detail.abstract: This study examines the influence of extreme weather events on stock market behavior in China, focusing on the Shanghai and Hong Kong Stock Exchanges. This article’s hypothesis is that local weather affects individual investors in Shanghai more significantly due to their short-term, speculative trading habits. In contrast, institutional investors in Hong Kong are less influenced by short-term considerations due to their long-term strategies and access to resources. The Glosten-Jagannathan-Runkle Generalized AutoRegressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GJR-GARCH) estimator can test the hypothesis under different market conditions and volatility clustering. The analysis utilizes daily financial and meteorological data from January 1, 2009, to December 31, 2023. The GJR-GARCH estimator incorporates variables such as air pressure, humidity, sunshine hours, and temperature. The results show that extreme weather has a more pronounced effect on the Shanghai market than the Hong Kong market. Furthermore, extreme weather events influence stock turnover and volatility more than stock returns, reflecting shifts in investment behavior. The hypothesis is further tested to determine whether it remains valid during bull and bear markets, which are emotionally charged periods. The hypothesis still holds, albeit with less pronounced effects. Thus, extreme weather can impact stock market performance, with the composition of investors playing a significant role.

title: Attention as Currency: Rethinking Relevant Market Analysis in Digital Competition Law
affiliations: O. P. Jindal Global University - Jindal Global Law School (JGLS) and O. P. Jindal Global University, Jindal Global Law School

detail.title: Attention as Currency: Rethinking Relevant Market Analysis in Digital Competition Law
detail.abstract:
Digital platforms today operate largely on zero-price business models where users do not pay with money, but with their time and attention. Traditional competition law tools, especially price-based tests such as the SSNIP, therefore struggle to capture market power and competitive harm in these markets. This paper argues that attention, rather than price or data, is the true unit of competition in digital ecosystems and should be treated as an independent and relevant market for antitrust analysis.

The paper first explains how attention functions as a scarce and tradeable economic resource and why the conventional characterisation of platforms as two-sided markets obscures real competitive dynamics. It then critiques the proposed alternatives to SSNIP, particularly the SSNIC and SSNDQ tests, and shows how their theoretical foundations remain flawed in zero-price and attention-driven markets. Building on these gaps, the paper proposes a fresh analytical framework centred on three new tools: the SSAINT (Small but Significant Attention Increase Non-Transient Test) for market definition, the Attention Elasticity of Substitution (AES) for measuring competitive pressure, and the Attention Switching Cost Index (ASCI) for assessing user lock-in.

Through case studies including WhatsApp, Google Android, and Meta/Giphy, the paper demonstrates how an attention-based approach better captures ecosystem dominance, network effects, and non-price harms that conventional tools often miss. It concludes by suggesting that competition law must formally recognise attention as an economic currency if it is to remain effective in regulating digital platform power

title: Impact of biochar and inorganic fertilizers rates on yield and yield components of maize at Bako Western Ethiopia
affiliations: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research, Haramaya University, Haramaya University and Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research

detail.title: Impact of biochar and inorganic fertilizers rates on yield and yield components of maize at Bako Western Ethiopia
detail.abstract: Soil acidity is a major constraint to maize production in western Ethiopia, where maize serves as the principal staple crop. This problem severely limits yield, threatening food security and farmers’ livelihoods. To mitigate soil acidity and enhance maize productivity, this study evaluated the combined application of biochar and inorganic fertilizers. A two-year field experiment (2023/24 and 2024/25) was conducted at Bako, western Ethiopia, using a randomized complete block design (RCBD) arranged in a factorial with three replications. Treatments included three rates of biochar (0, 5, and 10 t ha⁻¹), nitrogen (0, 46, and 92 kg ha⁻¹), and phosphorus (0, 34.5, and 69 kg ha⁻¹ P₂O₅). Key agronomic parameters were measured to assess treatment effects. The results revealed that the combined application of biochar and inorganic fertilizers significantly enhanced maize growth and yield. The treatment with 5 t ha⁻¹ biochar, 92 kg N ha⁻¹, and 69 kg P₂O₅ ha⁻¹ produced the highest grain yield (7.2 t ha⁻¹), leaf area index (3.3), number of kernels per ear (462.2), thousand-kernel weight (428.3 g), and total biomass (23.7 t ha⁻¹). The synergistic use of biochar and fertilizers improved soil fertility and reduced acidity, leading to increased productivity. These findings highlight the potential of integrated nutrient management combining biochar and inorganic fertilizers to improve maize yield and soil fertility in acidic soils of western Ethiopia. The application of 5 t ha⁻¹ biochar with 92 kg N and 69 kg P₂O₅ per hectare is recommended as the optimal combination for maize production in acid-prone areas. Extension and demonstration activities are essential to promote farmer awareness and adoption of this integrated approach.

title:
Skies of Suspicion
Global Chemtrail Narratives in an Age of Anxiety
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Skies of Suspicion
Global Chemtrail Narratives in an Age of Anxiety
detail.abstract:
Chemtrail conspiracy theories persist not because they possess explanatory power,
but because they convert environmental uncertainty and psychological vulnerability
into structured narratives of intentional control. Across continents̶from Brazil to
Germany, Kenya to India̶ordinary contrails are reinterpreted as evidence of
chemical spraying, population engineering or state-orchestrated climate
manipulation. This article examines why these beliefs endure despite overwhelming
scientific consensus. Drawing on recent studies from MIT Media Lab, Ipsos Global,
and the Cambridge Conspiracy Cognition Project, it argues that the proliferation of
chemtrail narratives emerges at the intersection of digital algorithmic amplification,
institutional mistrust, and growing climatic anxiety. High-arousal misinformation
spreads through social platforms at rates nearly quadruple that of neutral content,
allowing visually dramatic contrail images to flourish within online echo chambers.
Psychological research indicates that conspiratorial ideation increases during
periods of uncertainty, where individuals prefer narratives of deliberate
orchestration over confronting randomness or lack of control. The chemtrail theory
thus functions as an emotional coping mechanism: a symbolic framework that
transforms fear of environmental instability into accusations of human agency. The
article explores this dynamic as a global cultural phenomenon, tracing how
communities engage in collective meaning-making that reinforces belief systems
through shared decoding rituals. Ultimately, chemtrail persistence reveals a broader
crisis in public reasoning, where societal fragmentation and digital noise erode the
authority of scientific explanation, allowing conspiratorial worldviews to thrive
under the illusion of mastery, clarity, and control.

While economists once counted a nation's wealth by its physical assets—facto- ries, buildings, and machines—today's most valuable resources often exist only in human minds and digital code. title: National Budget 2026 (Bulgaria): Higher Salaries in Higher Education, but No Structural Reform -"Helicopter Money"
affiliations: University of National and World Economy (UNWE) - Department of Economics

detail.title: National Budget 2026 (Bulgaria): Higher Salaries in Higher Education, but No Structural Reform -"Helicopter Money"
detail.abstract: This paper critically examines the funding model of Bulgarian higher education in the context of the draft National Budget 2026. Although the budget allocates approximately €767 million to the sector-an increase of nearly 12% compared to 2025-the additional resources are directed primarily toward salaries and recurrent expenditures, without accompanying structural reform. The analysis identifies three systemic weaknesses: (1) the ineffective funding model of state universities, which fails to link subsidies to quality and labor market relevance; (2) persistently low research productivity, reflected in Bulgaria's absence from prestigious international rankings, weak citation impact, and limited technology transfer; and (3) the lack of alignment between university output and labor market demand, resulting in oversupply in low-cost fields and shortages in STEM and medical specialties. The paper argues that increased allocations without reform constitute "helicopter money" and do not enhance efficiency. It recommends three major reforms: (i) replacing the outdated "money follows the student" principle with performance-based financing tied to quality and employability; (ii) strengthening research standards through amendments to the Law on the Development of Academic Staff and raising doctoral requirements; and (iii) aligning higher education provision with labor market needs by operationalizing the National Map of Higher Education. Without such measures, Bulgaria risks continued marginalization in global academic competition and limited contribution of publicly funded science to national economic development.

detail.abstract: India is undergoing a rapid digital transformation, driven by rising internet penetration, mobile connectivity, and the expansion of digital financial ser- vices. At the heart of this transformation is Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), a set of digital systems which includes Aadhaar (digital ID), UPI (digital pay- ments), and DigiLocker (digital data storage). These systems serve as the foundation for various digital services, improving financial inclusion, streamlining governance, and enhancing access to social benefits. The government has actively promoted digitalization through initiatives like Dig- ital India, a nationwide program launched in 2015 to expand digital infra- structure, improve online service delivery, and promote digital literacy. How- ever, while these advancements promise inclusive growth, they also raise concerns about the persistence of (digital) inequalities. Gaps in access, af- fordability, and digital literacy continue to exclude large sections of the pop- ulation, particularly in rural areas and among women. (The rest omitted.)

detail.abstract: Earlier this year, following the inauguration of the second Trump administra- tion, one of the most consequential policy decisions was the announcement of significant cuts and halts to expenditures by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). In addition, the administration initi- ated a sweeping reconstruction that included the integration of USAID into the Department of State and the layoff of thousands of USAID employees and contractors worldwide. As the United States remains the world’s largest donor country, these measures—driven by domestic political debates, fiscal constraints, and shifting foreign policy priorities—have sent shockwaves through the global development community, leaving many recipient coun- tries and crisis zones facing acute uncertainty regarding both ongoing and future support. Several European countries have also announced ODA budget cuts.1 For example, France announced cuts totaling 2.1 billion eu- ros, which is equivalent to a 37% reduction compared to the 2024 figure. Germany’s draft budget proposed a reduction of 836 million euros, repre- senting a 12% decrease from 2024 levels. title: Everyday Governance of NbS: How Local Knowledge, Customary Authorities and State Agencies Co-produce Riparian Restoration in the Densu River Basin
affiliations: , Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana and Cranfield University

detail.title: Everyday Governance of NbS: How Local Knowledge, Customary Authorities and State Agencies Co-produce Riparian Restoration in the Densu River Basin
detail.abstract: The effective implementation of nature-based solutions (NbS) in river basins relies critically on navigating complex institutional mechanisms within contexts, typically defined by legal pluralism. This study examines the everyday governance of riparian restoration in Ghana’s Densu River Basin (DRB), a vital ecosystem under severe degradation from illegal mining and pollution. Moving beyond simplistic top-down analyses, we employ a qualitative interpretive case study approach, analyzing interviews from 30 participants across three distinct, yet interacting, governance systems: statutory agencies, customary authorities, and local communities. We utilize a conceptual framework based on the three dimensions of power—structural, instrumental, and discursive—to explain how environmental outcomes are co-produced. Findings reveal a core tension: while high local mobilization and resilient social networks drive synergistic action, corrosive antagonism undermines long-term sustainability. This antagonism stems from the state’s selective use of structural power for exclusion and its consistent use of discursive power to marginalize Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) as "superstition". fostering a profound legitimacy crisis. We propose a Pluralist Governance Interaction Model, arguing that the success of NbS is conditional upon institutionalizing power-sharing. This requires specific structural reforms, such as permanent committee seats for women and youth and epistemological parity between scientific and traditional knowledge systems, to transform resource asymmetry into durable, equitable environmental co-management.

reference: Afrindependent Institute Academic Paper No. 012/2025
title: Restoring Objective Morality: The Africonomics Refutation of Western Consequentialist Philosophies
affiliations: Afrindependent Institute

detail.title: Restoring Objective Morality: The Africonomics Refutation of Western Consequentialist Philosophies
detail.abstract: This paper examines and refutes the dominance of Western consequentialist philosophies—particularly utilitarianism, materialism, and positivism—that have shaped economics, the broader social sciences, and state policy across the modern world. These frameworks, based on outcome-based reasoning, are fundamentally flawed and dehumanizing. They reduce human beings to instruments of state or collective objectives, denying their inherent dignity, moral agency, and natural rights. Africonomics restores objective morality as the foundation of ethics and social sciences, grounding human action, social order, and governance in natural-moral law principles. By demonstrating that ethical capacity is intrinsic to human life, this paper reestablishes the inseparable unity between morality and civilization. It advances Africonomics as a human-centered, morally grounded alternative to the Western consequentialist and statist paradigm. By affirming the primacy of objective moral principles over expedient outcomes, Africonomics charts a path toward a truly civilized world rooted in respect for human dignity, liberty, and agency.

title: Post-Colonial Trade Across European and Non-European Colonizers
affiliations: Ghent University and Ghent University

detail.title: Post-Colonial Trade Across European and Non-European Colonizers
detail.abstract: Existing studies on post-colonial trade have primarily focused on the British and French colonizers, leaving limited evidence on other colonial powers.  Using a more comprehensive colonial history dataset covering all colonial relationships, we examine the impact of global colonial history on trade. We find that both European and non-European colonizers have positive trade effects with former colonies. However, the magnitude and persistence of these effects are substantially larger for non-European powers. While some non-European colonizers exhibit the same trade erosion following independence as their European counterparts, others seem to retain strong colonial linkages.

title: Bank Credit and Trade Credit: A New Perspective from Bank Regulatory Penalties
affiliations: Dongbei University of Finance and Economics, Dongbei University of Finance and Economics, Dongbei University of Finance and Economics (DUFE), Dongbei University of Finance and Economics and Dongbei University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Bank Credit and Trade Credit: A New Perspective from Bank Regulatory Penalties
detail.abstract: Prior research offers mixed findings on the relationship between bank credit and trade credit. Using a novel dataset of bank regulatory penalties in China from 2012 to 2022, this paper re-examines the substitution hypothesis between bank credit and trade credit. We find that firms in cities with more frequent bank penalties significantly increase their use of trade credit. Penalties constrain bank credit supply and lower firms’ overall financing costs, prompting a shift from bank credit toward trade credit. This effect is weaker for firms with limited bargaining power over suppliers and stronger when executives have relevant financial experience. Firms with higher inventories and lower operating cash flows respond more actively, as do those in regions with higher social trust and less banking competition. Overall, the findings offer new evidence for the substitution hypothesis by highlighting the role of bank regulatory penalties as a shock to credit supply.

title: The Corruption Tax: When a Few Bad Actors Make Everyone Pay
affiliations: OP Jindal Global University

detail.title: The Corruption Tax: When a Few Bad Actors Make Everyone Pay
detail.abstract: This paper develops a Bayesian model of credence-good markets in developing economies plagued by layered corruption: consumer theft, firm adulteration, and regulatory bribery. Consumers observe noisy quality signals and form tempered Bayesian posteriors about hidden adulteration, where parameter \(\gamma\) captures resistance to negative evidence. Even with low initial dishonesty, tempering sustains high-equilibrium adulteration rates, generating a systemic ``corruption tax" that raises prices and lowers realised quality, a burden borne primarily by honest firms and consumers. We characterise equilibrium conditions under which corruption persists or collapses, and use numerical simulations to show that transparent regulation, improved detection technologies, and reduced consumer skepticism sharply lower fraudulent behavior. The analysis underscores how small dishonest acts trigger self-reinforcing distrust, highlighting the critical role of transparency and credible enforcement in restoring market efficiency.

title: The 34% IRR Global Public Good: Early Investment in Direct Air Capture as Wright's Law Option Economics for Climate Stabilization
affiliations: Carbon Finance Labs

detail.title: The 34% IRR Global Public Good: Early Investment in Direct Air Capture as Wright's Law Option Economics for Climate Stabilization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I work for Carbon Finance Labs and owned by Oxy Low Carbon Ventures which also owns 1PointFive a direct capture company.
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: none. self activity over thanksgiving break.

detail.abstract: Early investment in direct air capture (DAC) represents a global public good with extraordinary returns. Applying venture capital option economics to Wright's Law learning curves, we find that accelerated DAC investment generates a 34% internal rate of return (IRR) when comparing $400 billion in early investment (2025-2035) against $6.2 trillion in avoided deployment costs through 2060. This return accrues as a global public good: reduced costs for achieving climate targets benefit all nations regardless of who funds the initial learning. We model country-level investment allocations proportional to GDP and find that the United States ($105B), European Union ($70B), and China ($67B) would bear the primary burden under equitable sharing. Returns manifest through two channels: (1) direct economic multiplier effects of 1.5x during construction and ongoing operations, and (2) avoided climate damages of $38 trillion annually by 2050 under business-asusual warming. A GDP-weighted $400B global investment generates estimated returns of $237B in direct economic activity plus $2-6T in avoided climate damages-a combined return exceeding 500% over 25 years.

title: Macroeconomic Consequences of the Spanish Transition to Democracy
affiliations: SUNY at Binghamton, Department of Economics and Binghamton University

detail.title: Macroeconomic Consequences of the Spanish Transition to Democracy
detail.abstract: This paper uses the multiple outcome synthetic control method to study themacroeconomic consequences of the Spanish transition to democracy that startedafter Francisco Francos death in 1975. We employ the Cobb-Douglas productionfunction and construct the counterfactuals for GDP, TFP, capital, and labor. We find that GDP per worker and TFP increased almost immediately after the transition; however, total employment declined, and GDP per capita initially decreased as a result. Actual GDP per capita caught up with the counterfactual by the late 1980s and exceeded it by about 15% during the 1990s.

title: The Timing of Blockchain Adoption for Corporate Social Responsibility Verification under Competition
affiliations: Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, Tianjin University of Finance and Economics and Tianjin University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: The Timing of Blockchain Adoption for Corporate Social Responsibility Verification under Competition
detail.abstract: This study examines strategic blockchain investment timing for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) verification in competitive markets under uncertainty. We develop a dynamic game-theoretic model integrating real options theory to analyze how firms choose between substantive and symbolic CSR and when to adopt blockchain for authentication. Our findings demonstrate that: (1) Competitor's greenwashing delays the firm's own blockchain investment under low market uncertainty due to increased option value of waiting, yet accelerates adoption under high uncertainty as firms race to verify claims and resolve consumer confusion. (2) A unique strategic equilibria across adoption scenarios are shaped by cost asymmetry, investment costs, and initial market size, with high investment costs paradoxically enabling cost-disadvantaged firms to preempt leaders. (3) Blockchain transparency reshapes CSR competition by enabling early adopters to pressure rivals toward substantive CSR, shifting market equilibrium toward authenticity. A case study using electric vehicle industry data validates our theoretical framework, offering strategic insights for managing CSR transparency under competitive pressure.

title: Estimation of Welfare Effects in Hedonic Difference-in-Differences The Case of School Redistricting∗
affiliations: University of Kentucky, South Dakota State University and University of Kentucky

detail.title: Estimation of Welfare Effects in Hedonic Difference-in-Differences The Case of School Redistricting∗

keywords: School Quality JEL Classification Codes: H4

detail.abstract: Difference-in-differences (DID) estimation that identifies the capitalization of amenities through changes in housing prices has been widely used. However, there are concerns about how to interpret the estimates of capitalization from DID as changes in welfare. We demonstrate theoretically and empirically how this divergence between capitalization and welfare arises, showing that it stems from violations of the Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (SUTVA) and the time-constant gradient assumption (TCGA). Following Banzhaf (2021), we estimate the capitalization of school redistricting in a DID framework that incorporates general equilibrium effects. When comparing estimates from our generalized DID model to the conventional DID model, we find significant differences in both the capitalization effects and welfare changes associated with the school redistricting.

title: SERAC v. Nigeria: Strengthening Environmental Protection Through Human Rights
affiliations: REVA University

detail.title: SERAC v. Nigeria: Strengthening Environmental Protection Through Human Rights
detail.abstract: Environmental protection is increasingly recognized as essential to human rights, serving as a precondition for fundamental rights like life and health. This evolving perspective has prompted policymakers, judges, and academics to reconsider the linkage between environmental deprivation and human rights. Recognizing a clean environment as integral to human rights enforcement enables analysis of how environmental harm contributes to rights violations and the effectiveness of legal frameworks in addressing these issues. This paper assesses the contribution of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights to environmental jurisprudence, specifically in the cases of SERAC and CESR v. Nigeria and Article 24 of the African Charter. It demonstrates how environmental protection has become the foundation of human rights law, helping to establish the value of the environment independent of its role in enabling the enjoyment of other rights.

title: Short-term Wind Power Forecasting Based on VMD-SSA-BiLSTM
affiliations: , , Changsha University of Science and Technology and

detail.title: Short-term Wind Power Forecasting Based on VMD-SSA-BiLSTM
detail.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is imperative for maintaining grid stability and secure operations. In order to enhance the precision of predictions, this paper introduces a hybrid short-term wind power estimation model that integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) neural networks. Firstly, the VMD (Velocity Mean Deviation) technique is employed to divide the initial power data into numerous stable modal components, thereby segregating noise from significant information. Subsequently, the Sparrow Search Algorithm optimises the essential hyperparameters of the BiLSTM network in order to determine the optimal network configuration. In the final step, the VMD-SSA-BiLSTM model is constructed, where each decomposed component is predicted separately and then combined to yield the final wind power forecast. A case study employing data relating to a wind turbine facility located in Hunan Province is presented for the purpose of simulation. The findings indicate that the model under discussion significantly reduces prediction errors in comparison with conventional forecasting methods, both in terms of accuracy and stability. This method has been shown to offer a promising resolution to the issue of short-term wind power estimation.

title: Global Natural Rubber Price Decline: Econometric, ML Analysis, and China Export Strategy
affiliations: Shenzhen Middle School of Mathematics and Physics and

detail.title: Global Natural Rubber Price Decline: Econometric, ML Analysis, and China Export Strategy
detail.abstract: In recent years, natural rubber has become an essential global strategic resource, yet holistic analysis of China's production, price fluctuations, and global influence remains limited. This study evaluates the global natural rubber market, identifies price drivers, predicts future trends, and assesses export opportunities for small-scale producers. The analysis combines a literature review with global trade data, ARIMAX and Random Forest forecasting, and a feasibility assessment of small-scale plantations in Xishuangbanna, China. Results indicate that price declines are driven by oversupply from Southeast Asia, slowing Chinese automotive demand, synthetic rubber substitution, and rising local costs. Forecasting reveals that long-term price weakness limits raw rubber competitiveness. However, niche export channels, such as latex concentrate and ESG-certified rubber, may offer viable opportunities. These findings provide a structured framework for investment decisions and revitalizing small-scale plantations.

title: DAOs (Decentralised Autonomous Organizations) and Emerging Technologies: Legal, Technical and Governance Perspectives
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: DAOs (Decentralised Autonomous Organizations) and Emerging Technologies: Legal, Technical and Governance Perspectives
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolving role of Decentralised Autonomous Organisations (DAOs) within emerging digital environments and evaluates how new technologies-particularly artificial intelligence, the metaverse, quantum computing and IoT-driven infrastructures-are reshaping their structure and operation. Rather than focusing solely on technical capabilities, the paper highlights the broader legal and governance implications that arise when decentralised systems intersect with rapidly advancing technologies. The analysis suggests that DAOs not only challenge traditional organisational and regulatory models, but also require a more nuanced discussion about accountability, data protection, security, and the future of digital governance. The paper argues that the interaction between decentralised decision-making, programmable smart contracts, and increasingly autonomous technologies will force legal frameworks to reconsider long-standing assumptions about agency and responsibility. At the same time, innovations such as quantum-resistant cryptography, mixed-reality interfaces and distributed artificial intelligence may allow DAOs to develop more resilient and participatory governance models. Overall, the study presents DAOs as a significant point of convergence between law, technology and social organisation, and contends that their long-term viability will depend on how effectively they adapt to new technical possibilities while responding to the regulatory and ethical challenges that accompany them.

title: The effect of mandatory short interest disclosure on managers’ disclosure decisions: Evidence from peer firms’ management forecasts
affiliations: The University of Kitakyushu and University of Tokyo - Graduate School of Economics

detail.title: The effect of mandatory short interest disclosure on managers’ disclosure decisions: Evidence from peer firms’ management forecasts
detail.abstract: We examine the effect of mandatory short interest disclosure on managers’ disclosure decisions, while focusing on peer firms’ management forecasts. We focus on the Japanese market, where the Financial Services Agency of the Japanese government introduced mandatory disclosure of short interests for all stocks listed on its exchange in 2008. We find that managers under the threat of short selling increase the frequency of their forecast revisions. The result suggests that managers attempt to mitigate information asymmetry to avoid short selling through improved disclosure. We also find that managers of overpriced firms increase the disclosure of bad news (downward forecast revisions). This suggests that managers are likely to increase the disclosure of bad news in order to correct overpricing and seek to avoid short selling. The results suggest that mandatory short interest disclosure improves the information environment of peer firms, supporting the effectiveness of the short selling disclosure regulation.

title: GIFF: Introducing Shallow Backpropagation into Forward-Forward-Based GNNs for Graph Classification
affiliations: South China University of Technology and South China University of Technology

detail.title: GIFF: Introducing Shallow Backpropagation into Forward-Forward-Based GNNs for Graph Classification
detail.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been widely applied in various real-world scenarios. Most GNNs are trained by the backpropagation (BP) algorithm. The Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm is an alternative training method for neural networks is proposed to address the limitations in biological plausibility and memory efficiency of BP. The Graph Forward-Forward algorithm first attempted to introduce the FF algorithm into graph classification task. However, the vanilla FF algorithm is much slower than BP and can capture limited information from the raw data. Besides, this work is limited to discussing the feasibility of training Graph Convolutional Networks. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes the Graph Integrated Forward-Forward (GIFF) algorithm, a novel training approach which improves the performance of FF-based GNNs. Specifically, GIFF integrates shallow backpropagation by combining adjacent layers into sub-networks, which allows the trained GNN model to capture more information from the data and saves the training time. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets and two types of GNN models reveal that our training approach outperforms the vanilla FF algorithm, and it consumes less memory than BP.

detail.title: Clinic Business Strategies under Reimbursement Constraints: A Cross-National Analysis of Profitable Models

detail.abstract: This study analyzes business strategies for small to mid-size outpatient clinics operating under strict reimbursement constraints in Japan. Using financial diagnostic methods, publicly available health system data, and anonymized case studies from several primary care clinics, the research identifies structural pressures created by fee schedules, regulatory limits, and regional demographic trends. The comparative analysis evaluates profitability drivers, cost structures, and operational efficiency while highlighting differences among clinics with varying management approaches. The findings demonstrate that reimbursement-dependent clinics face substantial limitations in revenue scalability and financial resilience, particularly in suburban regions. However, strategic optimization-such as service mix restructuring, task shifting, digitalization, and optimized cost control-can significantly improve financial stability. This framework offers a practical model for clinic owners and healthcare managers seeking sustainable operations under Japan's reimbursement-based system and contributes insights for cross-national comparisons of health-system-driven business constraints.

title: Trading off carbon pricing with flexible regulations
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Trading off carbon pricing with flexible regulations
detail.abstract: Climate policy to drive deep emissions reductions is often politically difficult to implement and keep in place at rising stringencies. Surveys and historical evidence show that carbon pricing in particular, although considered economically most efficient, is often strongly opposed. This study aims to provide useful information to policymakers by comparing the likely economic outcomes between two policy approaches when used to reach net-zero emissions by 2050: carbon pricing and a suite of flexible regulations. We use a general equilibrium model of Canada’s energy economy system to simulate both policy approaches, with efficient and inefficient versions of each. Our simulations suggest that, depending on design features of each policy approach, such as use of carbon pricing revenue or flexibility mechanisms in regulations, economic outcomes can be similar or diverge in the long-term. A highly flexible suite of regulations, if designed carefully, can allow marginal abatement costs to be equated across regions and economic sectors and might promote earlier adoption of low-carbon technologies to the ultimate benefit of the economy in later years. We provide a comparison of policy design features and a comparison of likely economic outcomes to help inform policymakers as they navigate the challenging trade-off between the economic efficiency and political acceptability of decarbonization policy options.

title: Environmental History, Archaeology, and Political Ecology of Climate Change Cross-Disciplinary Reflections on Boundaries, Borderlands, and Population Displacement in Perpetuity?

detail.title: Environmental History, Archaeology, and Political Ecology of Climate Change Cross-Disciplinary Reflections on Boundaries, Borderlands, and Population Displacement in Perpetuity?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This project did not involve human participants or identifiable personal data; therefore, ethics approval and written informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A. This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews the intersections of environmental history, archaeology, and political ecology to deepen our understanding of climate displacement and migration. Drawing upon stories, Viking sagas, and hadithi of ancient wisdom, it highlights how these disciplines offer complementary perspectives on human-environment interactions. Environmental history situates contemporary climate challenges within long-term historical trajectories, revealing how past environmental transformations shape present vulnerabilities. Archaeology provides material evidence of historical adaptive strategies, offering insights into the resilience and ingenuity of past societies facing ecological change. Political ecology illuminates the socioeconomic and power dynamics that mediate climate impacts, emphasizing how governance and policy frameworks influence migration outcomes. Through integrating these approaches, this review underscores the value of interdisciplinary research for informing evidence-based interventions that address climate-induced displacement. The paper contributes to ongoing debates in the Anthropocene, human-environment externalism, and the ethics of policy responses, advocating for frameworks that are both historically informed and socially just in mitigating the impacts of climate migration.

title: Beyond Coding: Open-Source Innovation Disclosure and Startup Growth
affiliations: University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School, The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics, National University of Singapore (NUS) and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Beyond Coding: Open-Source Innovation Disclosure and Startup Growth
detail.abstract: We investigate how open-source code releases influence startup growth, focusing on the strategic trade-off between transparency-driven innovation and exposure to proprietary and cybersecurity risks. Using a novel dataset linking startups to GitHub activity, we find that open-sourcing significantly boosts user adoption and engagement. To address endogeneity, we implement a matched difference-indifferences design and use the staggered rollout of GitHub Copilot as an instrument. The results suggest a plausibly causal relation between open-source code releases and startup growth, particularly for protocols with decentralized governance, venture backing, high-quality codebases, and active developer communities. However, open-source code releases also carry risks: increased exposure to cyberattacks and competitive imitation. For example, after Uniswap's license expired, its market dominance fell by over 50% amid a surge in copycat platforms. Open-source startups are also more likely to suffer future security breaches than their closed-source counterparts. However, they develop more new features following code releases, as well as exhibit positive longrun returns, suggesting an alignment of the investor base with long-term value creation of open-source innovation. Our study highlights a trade-off that startups must navigate as they go beyond coding to signal credibility and build success in highly collaborative markets.

title: Credit-Spread Timing between High-Yield Bonds and Treasuries: Timing HYG vs IEF with Price-Ratio and Return-Spread Signals

detail.title: Credit-Spread Timing between High-Yield Bonds and Treasuries: Timing HYG vs IEF with Price-Ratio and Return-Spread Signals

detail.abstract: I study a monthly rotation between high-yield credit (HYG) and 7-10Y Treasuries (IEF) using two transparent signals: (i) a price ratio versus its lookback moving average and (ii) a return-spread with a threshold. Tests use month-end data, realistic frictions (0.03% per side), position bounds (HYG 20-80%), and a 30% turnover cap; an optional macro "thermometer" tilts to IEF when HY-OAS is elevated or the 10Y-3M curve is inverted. Versus a 50/50 HYG/IEF benchmark, both signals improve long-run growth with controlled drawdowns. Full-grid robustness across LB ∈ {6, 9, 12, 18} and TH ∈ [-3%,+3%] shows a wide performance plateau. Final recommendation: RATIO with LB = 9 and TH = +1%, chosen for sitting in the middle of the plateau and offering a balanced trade-off between CAGR, Sharpe, and drawdowns.

title: Private Property and the Economic Teachings of the Early Church Fathers
affiliations: West Virginia University - College of Business & Economics

detail.title: Private Property and the Economic Teachings of the Early Church Fathers

publicationDetails.detailsText: On Morality, Human Behaviour, and Economics, ed. S. Kamall & J. Castaneda. Vinson Centre (forthcoming)

detail.abstract: The economic teachings of the early Church Fathers unequivocally encourage and command the rich to give their wealth to poor. Their words are rich and edifying; and in the Eastern Orthodox Church, they carry authority. It is tempting, from our modern political context, to take them to imply that Divine justice requires the redistribution of wealth across society, and radical reform of the legal and economic systems we live under to ensure that there be no vast inequality between the economic standing of members of society-perhaps even the abolition of private property. This chapter outlines and contextualise the teachings found in the homilies of St. Basil the Great and St. John Chrysostom, and argues that they call for no particular political programme of economic reform or revolution. Rather, they take for granted a legal system of property rights, and make commands upon individuals based upon how they fare within that system. There is no case for the abolition of private property to be found in these teachings.

detail.abstract: Climate refugee status is not currently established in international law. Evolving discourse on refugee determination and admissions systems, however, suggests that although climate change is not a legally admissible threat on its own, in the future it could be considered when reviewing refugee applications, particularly in circumstances where climate change has exacerbated conflicts. Drawing upon political ecology theory and international refugee law, and using case studies of state and international action on climate refugees, this paper develops criteria for appraising the susceptibility, level of exposure to, and ability to cope with climate change impacts that drive population displacement across borders. There are several frameworks for such Climate Risk Assessments (CRAs), but many of them are either too broad in the environmental variables that they analyze or inadvertently omit socio-ecological factors. The impacts of climate change are firstly not typically included among refugee vulnerability assessment, and secondly, they are less clear-cut than traditional sources of refugee claims, such as fleeing war, genocide or political persecution. For example, what constitutes an “immediate threat to life” in climate change contexts could result from the passing of a powerful tropical cyclone (sudden-onset), or take decades or more to unfold, like sea level rise (slow-onset). Perhaps homing in on the variables that factor the most in climate-induced migration across borders may contribute to establishing related criteria in the Refugee Determination Systems (RDS) used by nation-states and International Organizations that have refugee admission responsibilities.

title: The Consumption Structure Index (CSI): A Structural Framework for Diagnosing Poverty through Consumption

detail.title: The Consumption Structure Index (CSI): A Structural Framework for Diagnosing Poverty through Consumption
detail.abstract: Contemporary poverty is shaped not only by scarce resources but also by what households can do, display, and become. Material sufficiency can coexist with institutional detachment and limited recognition. However, current metrics compress these differences into additive shortfalls. This paper introduces the Consumption Structure Index (CSI), a role-based compositional approach that interprets deprivation as the patterned absence of role-bearing goods rather than income deficiency alone. The CSI distinguishes anchors, normal goods, and symbolic goods across six domains: nutrition, education, health, housing, communication, and social integration. Fixed roles encode hierarchies of institutional connection and symbolic legitimacy, while contextual benchmarking aligns items and thresholds with locally expected standards. The paper sets out the conceptual foundations and measurement structure of the CSI and outlines a blueprint for implementation. Empirical calibration and validation are left to future work.

title: Engineering a Quantum Phase Transition in Corporate Payouts: Evidence from Meta Platforms' "Year of Efficiency" and Dividend Initiation

detail.title: Engineering a Quantum Phase Transition in Corporate Payouts: Evidence from Meta Platforms' "Year of Efficiency" and Dividend Initiation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Quantumist.AI, a planned commercial venture focused on quantitative finance research and analytics. However, this research was conducted independently, and the findings, methodology, and conclusions were developed prior to and separate from any commercial considerations. The author holds no financial interests in Meta Platforms Inc., Alphabet Inc., or other entities discussed in this study, and received no compensation or funding from these companies. All data used in this analysis is derived from publicly available sources including SEC filings, earnings transcripts, and market data. The Quantum Capital Dynamics framework presented herein is an academic contribution developed through independent research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was conducted independently by the author as part of the Quantum Capital Dynamics research series. All costs associated with data acquisition, analysis, and publication were borne by the author.

detail.abstract:
Building on the Quantum Capital Dynamics framework established by Nayani (2025), this study analyzes Meta Platforms Inc. as a natural experiment in "engineered" quantum phase transitions. Unlike Alphabet Inc., which followed a linear evolution, Meta executed a dramatic regime shift between 2022 and 2024—transforming from a destructive interference state ($\theta \approx 165^\circ$, -26.4% crash) to a constructive entanglement state ($\theta\approx 38^\circ$, +20.3% surge). We apply the Quantum Interference Index (QII) to quantify how the "Year of Efficiency" narrative acted as a wave-function collapse mechanism, effectively tunneling the stock price through valuation resistance. Furthermore, we isolate the February 2024 dual-payout event (dividend initiation + $50B buyback) to measure the "cross-term coupling coefficient" ($\lambda \approx 0.35$), confirming that simultaneous payout signals generate non-linear value amplification (+15%) beyond the classical sum of parts.

This submission is the second installment in a longitudinal series on Quantum Capital Dynamics. The inaugural study, "Two-Particle Quantum Interference in Corporate Payouts: A Longitudinal Case Study of Alphabet Inc. (2019–2024)," was submitted to SSRN on November 27, 2025 (Abstract ID: 5818342).

title: A New Modeling Approach to Help Address the Trump Tariffs
affiliations: Kobe University and University of Cambridge - Wolfson College

detail.title: A New Modeling Approach to Help Address the Trump Tariffs
detail.abstract: In this paper, we show that the existing models and descriptions of the transfer of capital between countries that are provided in international economics are inadequate because they fail to explain the causes of, or the consequences of, persistent trade imbalances and because the assumption that there is a world interest rate, r* at which all countries can theoretically lend or borrow is extremely misleading. Instead, we argue that a more fruitful modeling approach is to regard the world as consisting of a number of regions, each of which has a particular rate of return on capital, which is a function of the local marginal product of capital (MPK). We demonstrate that such a modeling approach can provide some additional insights into who gains and loses from persistent trade deficits and how this might be affected by the Trump Administration's tariff policy.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bocharova, Irina & Rymanov, Alexander (2025). Novedades en Población, 21(42).

detail.abstract: The study examines the factors that facilitate the transmission of the coronavirus in Russian public long-term care facilities due to overcrowding. All types of adult care facilities were exposed to an elevated risk of infection with the novel coronavirus during the global pandemic. These factors include (A) a high average number of residents, (B) an increase in the number of residents during the pandemic, and (C) a failure to comply with the standard for the provision of floor space. These risk factors were especially prevalent in psychoneurological boarding schools for adults and special boarding homes. Spatial estimates indicate that at the onset of the coronavirus pandemic, 12% of the country's regions were experiencing overcrowding in public long-term care facilities, which had a deleterious impact on the implementation of measures to prevent the emergence and spread of the coronavirus infection. At the onset of the coronavirus pandemic, disparities between regions reached a maximum level in comparison to the pre-pandemic and late-pandemic periods.

title: Belief Segmentation and Price-Discrimination in Equivalent Currency Markets
affiliations: Lund University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Belief Segmentation and Price-Discrimination in Equivalent Currency Markets
detail.abstract: Why do mispricings persist even when assets are legally fungible and arbitrage faces no regulatory or convertibility constraints? This paper develops a two-market OTC-dealer framework showing that belief heterogeneity in investors alone can sustain persistent cross-market wedges in an OTC dealer-setting. Investor heterogeneity allows for third-degree price discrimination from market makers. Empirical evidence, utilizing high frequency data, through a DiD setup , threshold analysis and event studies supports the mechanism and is robust to different empirical specifications. In markets shaped by distorted beliefs, mispricings persists not because of technological limitations but due to dealers exploiting investor beliefs.

title: Immigration Enforcement in the 2025 Era: Constitutional Concerns, Economic Impacts, and Implementation Failures

detail.title: Immigration Enforcement in the 2025 Era: Constitutional Concerns, Economic Impacts, and Implementation Failures
detail.abstract: Since January 2025, the Trump administration has implemented one of the most aggressive immigration enforcement campaigns in modern U.S. history, characterized by quota-driven arrests, elimination of sensitive location protections, and courthouse-based apprehension tactics. This white paper examines the constitutional, economic, and operational dimensions of these policies through the lens of documented incidents and empirical data. We analyze three critical failures: (1) constitutional violations resulting from racial profiling and wrongful detention of U.S. citizens; (2) economic contradictions whereby deportation of taxpaying workers accelerates Social Security insolvency; and (3) catastrophic implementation marked by quota systems that incentivize quantity over public safety priorities. Drawing on government statistics, legal cases, and healthcare system data, we document how enforcement tactics including hospital arrests, courthouse entrapment, and ICE impersonation crimes have created public health crises and destroyed community trust in legal institutions. The analysis reveals a fundamental tension between stated policy objectives and actual outcomes, with enforcement methods that paradoxically undermine both border security goals and fiscal sustainability while violating Fourth Amendment protections.

title: Balancing Growth and Conservation: The Economic Impact of Environmental Enforcement in the Brazilian Amazon
affiliations: University of Bonn, University of Bonn - Center for Development Research (ZEF) and University of Bonn

detail.title: Balancing Growth and Conservation: The Economic Impact of Environmental Enforcement in the Brazilian Amazon
detail.abstract: This paper examines the causal economic impacts of environmental enforcement in the Brazilian Amazon between 2002 and 2016. Using an instrumental variable strategy that exploits exogenous variation in satellite monitoring capacity from cloud cover, we show that stricter enforcement by the federal environmental agency IBAMA significantly reduces deforestation and pasture expansion while shifting agriculture towards soy cultivation. These land-use changes are accompanied by higher soy sector employment, wages, and productivity, without measurable losses in agricultural GDP. However, enforcement reduces the number of rural credit contracts and leads to a notable contraction in municipal public administration jobs. The results indicate that well-targeted enforcement can redirect economic activity towards more intensive and sustainable production without sacrificing output, but complementary measures, such as tailored credit access and technical support are important to address adjustment costs and ensure inclusive gains.

detail.abstract: Sustainable procurement is a growing strategic priority across various sectors. Yet, its implementation in educational supply chains, particularly in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), remains constrained. Educational institutions in the UAE engage in complex procurement processes encompassing uniforms, textbooks, technology, transportation, facilities management, and contractual services. This study establishes a pragmatic framework for incorporating sustainable procurement practices into UAE school supply chains by analysing four prominent educational organisations: SABIS/International Schools of Choueifat (ISC), GEMS Education, Aldar Academies, and Taaleem. A mixedmethod approach was employed, including semi-structured interviews with procurement professionals and a descriptive survey of school operations teams. Findings indicate restricted environmental assessment criteria, cost-centric decision-making practices, uneven sustainability reporting by suppliers, and operational obstacles including pressing schedules and disjointed stakeholder alignment. The study introduces the Sustainable Procurement Alignment Framework (SPAF) comprising three pillars that integrate environmental, economic, and operational dimensions. This framework provides UAE schools with a systematic approach to enhance procurement transparency, strengthen decision-making processes, and generate sustainable value.

title: Intellectual Property and Competition in the Age of Surveillance Capitalism: Protecting Innovation or Entrenching Monopoly?
affiliations: and  Llyod School of law

detail.title: Intellectual Property and Competition in the Age of Surveillance Capitalism: Protecting Innovation or Entrenching Monopoly?
detail.abstract:
The evolution of surveillance capitalism has created a structural change in market power by converting human experience into a raw resource to be extracted, analysed, and shaped into predictable behaviour. This dates back to targeted advertising in early 2000s when economic order flourished on behavioural overabundance, data gathered beyond service requirements is processed into prediction-based products and sold in behavioural futures markets. Although there are people who argue that the industry will improve consumer welfare by facilitating personalization, efficiency and innovation, the very logic behind this is deeply flawed in terms of market fairness, privacy and democratic integrity.[1]

The State of data-driven economy with its market dominance is achieved by few technology conglomerates through network effects, asymmetries of data, and algorithmic opacity to develop sustainable market power, leading to so-called epistemic inequality. Such economic control enables to shape consumer preferences and politics discourse through the manipulative approach, blurring difference between competition and behavioural control.[2] On this background, this paper addresses How power of knowledge and ability to control market competition and consumer choice skewed when concentrated in powerful technology companies? and What are the extent of competition law frameworks of existing data exploitation as consumer harm besides price measures?

The paper examines surveillance capitalism within existing legal provisions of competition policy and proposes reform to incorporate the data governance in the competition policy regulation, make algorithms transparent, prevent exploitive behavioural markets, and acknowledge the right on the personal data protection as an indissoluble realm of customer protection. The anticipated result is a redesigned approach to competition law, a shift from perhaps-consent-based model to metric-based approach, which can counter not only harms but also the economically efficient processes, as well as the democratic things, which are at stake in the era of widespread data exploitation

title: Working Paper 25-1 Trump's Global Tariff War: Faulty Premises, Costly Consequences
affiliations: Economics International Inc

detail.title: Working Paper 25-1 Trump's Global Tariff War: Faulty Premises, Costly Consequences
detail.abstract: The Trump Global Tariff War (TGTW) has discarded US commitments to the postwar international trading order established under the GATT and WTO. It replaces the Most Favored Nation principle with an "Every Nation Different" principle under the false premise that any economy with a trade surplus against the United States must be cheating on its trade obligations, and imposes a "reciprocal" tariff increase based on the ratio of bilateral US imports to exports. It fails to recognize the role of US fiscal deficits in boosting demand for imports, and of the attractiveness of the US capital market to inflows of foreign capital in strengthening the dollar and contributing to a persistent trade deficit. The TGTW promises revival of US manufacturing jobs under the false premise that trade deficits rather than technological change and Engels Curve shifts in demand toward services have driven the decline in the share of manufacturing in employment and GDP. It shows no recognition that higher tariffs are a self-inflicted wound to the economy because of large static welfare triangle costs and loss in dynamic efficiency growth. This study estimates that the 18 percent rise in tariffs so far in the TGTW imposes an ongoing future static welfare cost of 0.28 percent of GDP. The medium-term dynamic efficiency loss brings the total welfare loss reaching a range of 1.1 to 2.3 percent of baseline GDP by 2035. CBO budget estimates of increased tariff revenue of 1 percent of GDP over the next decade (including interest savings) may be understated on an implied premise of sharp import reductions but overstated because President Trump has suggested giving them away in "tariff dividend" checks to all but high-income households. Moreover, a possible Supreme Court ruling against application of the "emergency" legislation on which the main tariff increases are based further reduces the reliability of revenue estimates. The TGTW has usefully revealed a vulnerability of the US economy to a future cutoff in the supply of rare earth minerals, metals, and magnets imported from China that requires urgent action.

detail.abstract: This research interrogates the geopolitical and economic configurations perpetuating systemic inequities within the contemporary international order. It critically analyses how hegemonic powers, particularly the United States, engineer structural dependencies across the Global South to consolidate economic and strategic supremacy. Through the prism of alleged U.S. involvement in the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, it elucidates the entanglement of asymmetrical trade regimes, militarized capital flows, and techno-imperial monopolies that erode India's sovereign autonomy. The study culminates policy interventions aimed at revitalizing democratic sovereignty, resisting sectarian nationalism, and envisioning a de-colonial, normatively just architecture of global governance.

detail.abstract: The drive towards economic sustainability with reduced inequality, hunger, and poverty remains part of the United Nations development goals, known as SDG, aimed to be achieved by 2030. In Nigeria, rural poverty is still high at 75.5%, and food insecurity and starvation highlight the ongoing effects of terrorism and herder-farmer conflicts in the country's middle belt. This persistent troubling situation emphasises the need to reassess the pursuit of sustainable and inclusive growth in light of globalisation. The findings indicate that trade openness has little relation to sustainable economic growth in Nigeria, raising questions about the impact of increased economic integration, freetrade zones, and regional alliances on human development. The study suggests a need for a structural development framework adapted to the country's economic context, focusing on human capacity in artificial intelligence, wider adoption of automation, and an overhaul of the nation's outdated administrative system, to foster sustainable growth driven by improved institutional quality.

title: From Cartels and Militias to States and Markets: Stabilization as a Generational Exit Strategy
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: From Cartels and Militias to States and Markets: Stabilization as a Generational Exit Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural dynamics that allow cartels and terrorist organizations to become entrenched in fragile states, with a particular focus on how these groups act as de facto employers, protectors, and governors. Through a comparative analysis of regions such as Venezuela, Mexico, Afghanistan, Syria, and the Sahel, it explores how weak, predatory, or absent states create conditions where illicit groups provide essential services, employment, and security. The paper introduces a novel framework of generational dependency, proposing that reliance on illicit actors becomes normalized over time and passed down through generations, creating a cycle of economic and ideological dependence. The paper argues that long-term stabilization efforts—rooted in economic development, social services, and the restoration of state legitimacy—can disrupt this cycle. By integrating micro-level research on individual decision-making, community dynamics, and the generational transmission of norms, the paper highlights the need for comprehensive stabilization strategies that address both material and ideological factors. Furthermore, it calls for cross-regional research to understand the nuances of these dynamics and emphasizes the importance of international cooperation and domestic governance in implementing long-term solutions. Ultimately, this paper advocates for a holistic, multi-sectoral approach to reducing the influence of illicit groups, offering a framework for both scholars and policymakers working to stabilize fragile states.

title: Implementation of AI in FinTech: How Kazakhstan's Digital Leap is Redefining Financial Efficiency
affiliations: Municipal State Institution Specialized Gymnasium No 12 Named After Shokan Ualikhanov

detail.title: Implementation of AI in FinTech: How Kazakhstan's Digital Leap is Redefining Financial Efficiency
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping financial technology at an accelerating pace, fundamentally altering how individuals access, manage, and transact money. This paper investigates the implementation of AI in FinTech through the case of Kazakhstan, where rapid digital transformation has redefined financial efficiency. At the center of this shift is Kaspi.kz-a domestically developed super-app that integrates banking, e-commerce, travel booking, and instant payments into a single platform. Unlike traditional financial systems in many developed nations-where interbank transfers often take 1-3 business days-Kaspi enables peer-to-peer transactions in under five seconds, powered by real-time processing and AI automation. The platform delivers AI-driven credit decisions in less than 60 seconds, serving over 9 million active users as of early 2025, according to its investor reports. Customer support is streamlined through hybrid chatbots combining artificial intelligence with human oversight, drastically reducing wait times and operational costs. On October 31, 2025, Kaspi launched Kaspi.Alaqan, a palm-vein biometric payment system allowing contactless transactions without smartphones, cards, or internet connectivity-one of the first commercial deployments of its kind worldwide. By analyzing these innovations, this research demonstrates how AI enhances financial outputs without increasing inputs, significantly improving speed, security, and scalability. The study further explores how such advancements can expand financial inclusion, reduce transaction friction, and generate high-value employment in tech, data science, and cybersecurity. As legacy systems struggle with inefficiency, Kazakhstan's experience offers a compelling model for emerging economies aiming to leapfrog outdated infrastructure. The evidence suggests that AI-powered FinTech is not merely an incremental improvement but a foundational evolution toward faster, more inclusive, and user-centric finance.

title: Global Trade: A Comprehensive Review
affiliations: and Universidad Europea de Madrid

detail.title: Global Trade: A Comprehensive Review
detail.abstract: The cross-border exchange of goods, services, capital, and knowledge has turned up as a crucial driver of economic growth. The objective of this work is to contribute with an analysis of research trends in foreign and international trade, analyzing thematic gaps and highlighting areas for future research. To this end, a scientometric evaluation and a systematic literature review of Scopus publications from the previous five years are conducted. The results reveal an important growth in current academic production, with the academic articles predominantly in English. Furthermore, policy formulation requires a comprehensive approach, balancing free markets and protectionism, and promoting participation in trade agreements and free trade treaties that foster multilateral and bilateral integration. Furthermore, investment in infrastructure, logistics, and technological innovation, as well as examining and understanding of socioeconomic, cultural, health, and environmental factors, can improve connectivity and efficiency in trade. However, given the environmental impact of trade, trends have emerged that seek a balance between trade and environmental preservation and socioeconomic inequality.

title: The Alchemists of the Academy: A Popperian Critique of the "Forced Growth" in Modern Science
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Alchemists of the Academy: A Popperian Critique of the "Forced Growth" in Modern Science
detail.abstract: This essay reflects on Rafe Champion's The Two Faces of Karl Popper through the lens of contemporary scientific stagnation. It argues that modern institutional science has betrayed the true spirit of discovery-defined by spontaneous, nature-driven free thought-in favor of a bureaucratic consensus model. This phenomenon serves as an intellectual "pulling up of seedlings to help them grow," where funding mechanisms and SCI metrics induce artificial curiosity and prioritize the accumulation of experimental data over theoretical insight. Drawing comparisons between the theoretical triumphs of the Newtonian era and the "data-piling" of modern research, the essay posits that current academia has regressed into a form of high-tech alchemy. It concludes that without a return to the primacy of theory and the logic of scientific deduction, we face a "New Dark Age" of academic conformity.

detail.abstract: We examine the role of owner-occupied housing for income inequality. Departing from related work, we incorporate accrued capital gains, focus on long-run measures of income, and consider implications for tax progressivity. Using Australia as a case study, we show that housing income can have major implications for the apparent level and trends over time of inequality, progressivity of taxes and transfers, as well as the demographic profile of the rich and the poor. When imputed rent and accrued capital gains—neither of which are taxed—are included in the income base, the redistributive impact of income tax is reduced by 40%.

title: Are Shareholder and Debtholder Monitoring Substitutes or Complements? Causal Evidence from Russell Index Reconstitutions and Debt Maturity
affiliations: King’s College London, King's College London and Southwest University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Are Shareholder and Debtholder Monitoring Substitutes or Complements? Causal Evidence from Russell Index Reconstitutions and Debt Maturity
detail.abstract: This study explores whether the monitoring roles of passive shareholders and debtholders are substitutes or complements in affecting corporate debt maturity structure. We find that firms with an exogenous increase in passive ownership from the Russell 1000/2000 index reconstitution utilize a higher proportion of long-term debt. The impact is larger for firms with weak governance, greater information asymmetry, and higher liquidity risk. Furthermore, firms with increased passive ownership tend to issue more long-term debt, indicating lenders' increased willingness to provide long-term capital. Overall, our findings suggest that passive ownership can substitute short-term debt by enhancing monitoring and improving information environment.

detail.abstract: Nigeria's attempts to alleviate poverty and achieve sustainable development often fall short due to ongoing economic and political challenges in various sectors. This study explores the complex obstacles that impede the country's sustainable economic growth over time. Focusing on Nigeria's progress towards equitable growth from 1981 to 2024, the research examines how inclusive growth impacts real GDP and explores its longterm relationship. Using Ordinary Least Squares regression, the study reveals that both Gross Fixed Capital Formation and Foreign Direct Investment notably promote economic growth, while government expenditure, though positive, has a limited influence. Based on these findings, the study recommends adopting a more inclusive development approach that tackles Nigeria's diverse challenges, highlighting ethnoregional frameworks, increased FDI, and enhanced government social spending.

detail.abstract: Poverty and inequality remain widespread in regional Nigeria, with the Northern part of the country facing a disproportionate share due to population explosion, higher poverty rates, and greater inequality. Currently, Nigeria faces multiple crises, including regional agitation, insecurity, and terrorism, while hunger and starvation persist, leading citizens to protest repeatedly. This paper argues that population growth and the consumer price index are pivotal forces influencing sustainable growth in Nigeria between 1990 and 2024. The central argument is that population growth is a significant barrier to sustainable, inclusive growth. Empirical evidence, supported by previous research, indicates that population growth is a key factor hindering the nation's development goals. The recommendation is a systematic regional approach to eliminate widespread poverty, which contributes to rapid population growth, by creating tailored educational frameworks that account for ethno-regional and religious densities and incentivising programme participation through stipends.

detail.abstract: This year, 2025, marks the 60th anniversary of the normalization of diplo- matic relations between the Republic of Korea (ROK) and Japan. The ROK and Japan normalized their diplomatic relations by signing the Treaty on Basic Relations between ROK and Japan in June 1965. During the Cold War, the United States sought to establish a liberal bloc within East Asia, centered on Japan, to counter the communist bloc, toward which it pursued the normalization of ROK-Japan relations. Following its loss in World War II, Japan needed to resolve postwar issues through normalization of diplomatic relations with the ROK, while the ROK was in dire need of foreign capital necessary for its economic growth. Against this background, ROK-Japan diplomatic relations were normalized in 1965. (The rest omitted.)
